verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an entity providing information to a competent supervisory authority in connection with an incident or breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to proactively notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach, subject to a risk exception, without undue delay and normally within 72 hours. Norm B requires non-micro financial entities to provide, only upon the authorities’ request, an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses resulting from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The substantive compliance actions differ: mandatory incident notification within a fixed deadline versus on-request provision of a cost-and-loss estimate, with different triggering conditions and information content.

verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het beheersen van ICT-/beveiligingsrisico’s door organisatorische of technische maatregelen, maar de concrete verplichte handeling verschilt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist dat aanbieders passende en evenredige maatregelen nemen om beveiligingsrisico’s en de gevolgen van incidenten te beperken. Norm B vereist dat een bestaand ICT-risicobeheerkader periodiek en bij ernstige incidenten wordt gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, voortdurend wordt verbeterd, en op verzoek aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt verstrekt.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde compliance-actie: A betreft het implementeren en onderhouden van risicobeperkende beveiligingsmaatregelen; B betreft documentatie, evaluatie, voortdurende verbetering en mogelijke indiening van een risicobeheerkader.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by a relevant incident or abnormal event and concern timely handling or detection of ICT/data-related problems.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach within the specified timeframe (with reasons for delay). Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for detecting abnormal activities, ICT incidents, network-performance issues, and physical single points of failure; it does not require notifying an authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: external regulatory notification versus maintaining and testing internal detection mechanisms.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren, met inbegrip van kwesties op het gebied van ICT-netwerkprestaties en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, en om potentiële zwakke fysieke punten (“single points of failure”) te identificeren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require action to be taken promptly after awareness of a serious incident: Norm A requires notifying affected clients, while Norm B requires making a regulatory incident report, with a specific outer deadline in the event of death.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The required recipient and substantive action differ: Norm A is client-facing communication about the incident and mitigation measures (or protective measures for a significant cyber threat); Norm B is an incident notification/report to the competent authority or designated reporting channel under the AI Act, triggered by a causal link or suspected causal link and subject to a ten-day maximum in the death case.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different compliance action and recipient: client notification versus formal serious-incident reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations triggered in connection with ICT or network-and-information-system risks and addressed to entities in the digital/financial sector.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an entity, when ordered by the minister, to use only products or services from suppliers other than a minister-designated risky party, potentially including replacement or termination of existing products or services. Norm B requires non-micro financial entities, upon request by competent authorities, to provide an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents. One is a supplier/product exclusion and procurement or replacement obligation; the other is an information-reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world compliance actions are substantively different: supplier restriction/replacement versus furnishing a cost-and-loss estimate to authorities.

verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting a qualifying security/safety incident to a designated public authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the public body or designated organization to notify the Minister without delay of breaches or misuse involving its own electronic service and to provide all necessary information. Norm B requires reporting specified serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where the incident occurred; its scope is limited to the incidents defined in Article 3(49)(c). The reporting recipient, incident scope, and contextual conditions therefore differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in substantive scope and recipient: immediate notification to the Minister concerning the addressee's own electronic-service security/integrity or access misuse, versus reporting narrowly defined serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems to the territorially designated national competent authority.

verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to implement or use security-related technical/ICT measures aimed at preventing or reducing cybersecurity risks and their effects.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires public electronic communications providers to adopt technical, operational, and organisational measures to manage network or service security risks and limit the consequences of security incidents, specifically with regard to national security or public order. Norm B requires financial entities to use ICT technologies and processes that protect data and prevent specific data-security failures, including loss of availability, compromised authenticity or integrity, confidentiality breaches, and data loss. The obligations overlap at a high level but differ in regulated subject matter, addressees, and the concrete security outcomes required.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: A is a broad organisational and operational risk-management duty for securing communications networks/services and mitigating incident consequences, while B is a data-protection and ICT-control duty focused on preventing enumerated data-security failures.

verdict.evidence_span_b: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to an incident or breach identified during operation/testing by communicating information to a public authority. However, this is only a broad incident-notification theme, not the same complete compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a data-breach notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and affected person(s), including the breach's nature, information sources, recommended mitigation measures, and—toward the authority—consequences and measures taken or proposed. Norm B requires reporting each serious incident found during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority under Article 73, alongside immediate risk mitigation, suspension, or termination of testing and a recall procedure if testing is terminated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in regulated subject matter, recipients, required content, and accompanying operational measures: personal-data-breach notification and victim communication versus serious-AI-incident reporting to market surveillance with immediate testing-risk controls and possible recall.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take action after a serious ICT/AI incident, but the required actions are not the same: Norm A requires post-incident evaluation and, on request, reporting implemented changes to competent authorities; Norm B requires the provider to promptly investigate the serious incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities and preserving the system for later causal evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a retrospective post-incident evaluation and possible disclosure of resulting changes, whereas Norm B is an immediate substantive investigation of the incident and system, including risk assessment and corrective action, with procedural safeguards against altering the system before causal evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core compliance actions differ in substance: communicating changes resulting from a post-incident evaluation versus promptly conducting an investigation with risk assessment and corrective measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating certain ICT/data incidents or vulnerabilities to affected external parties, but they do not require the same operational measure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a direct, prompt notification duty on the provider toward the individual whose personal data are affected by a qualifying personal-data breach. Norm B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of at least serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public; it is a preparedness/planning obligation, not necessarily an immediate notification of a particular affected person or incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: immediate individual breach notification versus maintaining a crisis-communication plan for responsible disclosure to a broader set of stakeholders.

verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant provider (or an authorized representative acting on its behalf) to provide information requested by the competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B additionally requires authorized representatives of certain providers to grant the requested access, whereas Norm A expressly preserves the critical ICT third-party provider’s full responsibility for incomplete, inaccurate, or misleading information and permits lawyers to submit it on the client’s behalf.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core information-supply action is substantially the same, but Norm B includes a distinct access-granting obligation and Norm A includes an express continuing-responsibility rule; these are substantive differences in the compliance duties as stated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De vertegenwoordigers van de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten verstrekken de gevraagde informatie.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieders van AI-modellen voor algemene doeleinden of hun vertegenwoordiger verstrekken de gevraagde informatie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern prompt reporting of a qualifying security incident, but they require different substantive communications to different recipients.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an early warning to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident-characterisation information and the responsible officer’s contact details. Norm B requires the public electronic communications service provider to notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority immediately of a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required recipient and the substance of the notification differ: Norm A is an early-warning communication with incident details to cybersecurity authorities/CSIRT, whereas Norm B is a personal-data breach notification to the data-protection authority.

verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a compliance-related action following a triggering event, but the actions are materially different: Norm A requires performing checks/reconciliations to preserve data integrity during ICT-incident recovery, whereas Norm B requires submitting a report about a serious AI incident within a specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a substantive data-integrity verification and reconciliation duty during recovery; Norm B imposes an incident-reporting duty, with immediate reporting upon establishing or suspecting causation and an outside ten-day deadline in the specified fatality scenario.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are different in substance: operational verification of recovered or reconstructed data versus notification/reporting of a serious incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to maintain a record concerning qualifying digital/security incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires documenting personal-data breaches, including their facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so supervisory compliance can be checked. Norm B requires registering ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats as part of a broader incident-management process, including monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and addressing underlying causes. The scope and substantive incident-management obligations therefore differ.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required records concern overlapping but materially different subject matter and functions: breach documentation for supervisory verification versus registration embedded in an integrated ICT-incident management and root-cause-remediation process.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to communicate information to a public/regulatory authority or responsible body after a specified event.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a processor to promptly notify the controller of a personal-data breach. Norm B requires a deployer to notify the market-surveillance authority of the results of a prior fundamental-rights impact assessment and submit a completed template; it is a substantive reporting duty with prescribed content, not a breach alert to another responsible party.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: breach notification to a controller versus regulatory reporting of an impact-assessment outcome with a mandatory template.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following a serious ICT-related event, but their required compliance actions are not the same: Norm A requires the financial entity to conduct a post-incident evaluation, analyze causes, and identify improvements; Norm B requires reporting a serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority, alongside immediate mitigation, suspension, or termination of testing and a recall procedure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal post-incident review and improvement obligation. Norm B is an external incident-reporting and immediate risk-control obligation during real-world AI testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: internal evaluation and remediation planning versus regulatory notification and immediate containment/testing cessation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid als bedoeld in artikel 11.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to make a report concerning a qualifying incident, but they do not require the same reporting act in practice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires reporting a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, with a special death-related trigger and a maximum ten-day deadline after awareness. Norm B requires banks and specified financial-market entities to submit the relevant ICT-incident report (including a voluntary report) additionally to the designated sectoral CSIRT; its distinctive obligation is the extra reporting recipient and it concerns ICT incidents under the referenced regulation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share incident reporting as a broad compliance category, but differ in the substantive incident regime and especially in the required reporting destination: A sets the timing and trigger for an AI serious-incident report, while B imposes an additional report to a designated financial-sector CSIRT.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen vereisen dat een incident/inbreuk aan een bevoegde overheidsinstantie wordt gemeld, met een korte termijn die begint wanneer de meldingsplichtige zich van het incident bewust wordt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to serious ICT/AI-related incidents through incident-related communication or reporting.

Norm B requires the AI provider or deployer to make an actual report about a serious incident, subject to an immediate-trigger and maximum ten-day deadline where a person dies; it is not merely a planning or disclosure-capability obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to provide information to a competent authority, but the required information and the triggering/procedural context differ.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an incident notification to both the CSIRT and competent authority, generally within 72 hours (or 24 hours for the specified trust-service provider exception), including incident updates, an initial assessment, indicators of compromise where available, and information about cross-border effects. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding promptly to a data or ICT-related risk/incident, but they require different operational measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het reageren op cyber-/ICT-bedreigingen of -incidenten en noemen communicatie of opvolging na een trigger, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling op.

Norm B betreft de toezichthouder die ontvangst bevestigt en eventueel feedback of richtsnoeren verstrekt; daarnaast bevestigt zij dat financiële entiteiten verantwoordelijk blijven voor de behandeling en gevolgen van gemelde ICT-incidenten. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve organizational action concerning ICT/digital-risk governance or incident-related information handling by entities subject to the instruments.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to take organizational/operational steps related to cybersecurity risks and incidents, including preparing to understand or mitigate their effects.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires providers to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organizational security measures—potentially including encryption—to manage service-security risks and minimize incident impacts. Norm B requires financial entities to maintain capabilities and personnel specifically to collect information about vulnerabilities, cyber threats, and ICT incidents and analyze their likely effects on digital operational resilience. The former is a broad protective-control obligation; the latter is an intelligence, resourcing, and analytical-capability obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: implementing security safeguards versus maintaining resources and capabilities for threat/incident information gathering and impact analysis.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by a serious ICT/data incident and involve action by the regulated organization, but their required actions are different: Norm A requires promptly notifying the affected data subject of a personal-data breach, whereas Norm B requires documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework at least annually and in specified circumstances, with a report to the competent authority on request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to submit a legally relevant notification or report to a designated public authority/body.

The subject matter and compliance purpose differ: fundamental-rights assessment results versus ICT-incident reporting, and Norm A includes a prescribed completed template.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen voorzien in het verstrekken van informatie aan een overheidsinstantie naar aanleiding van een ICT-gerelateerde gebeurtenis.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to report an incident to a competent authority, but the reporting duties are not substantially identical in practice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an immediate preliminary warning to both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, within 24 hours, with specified preliminary information. Norm B requires financial entities to submit a structured sequence of initial, updated/interim, and final reports to the relevant competent authority within Article 20 deadlines, after collecting and analysing information; the authority may then disseminate details to other bodies.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a compliance action following an ICT incident or disruption, but the actions are materially different: Norm A requires periodic reporting to ENISA, whereas Norm B requires an internal post-incident evaluation and improvement analysis.

verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: external periodic regulatory reporting versus internal post-incident review and remediation planning.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require action in response to cybersecurity risks or incidents affecting digital systems/data, but they do not require the same operational compliance measure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours of becoming aware of it. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to take ongoing measures addressing ICT/security risks: Norm A requires implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures, while Norm B requires continuously identifying ICT-risk sources and assessing relevant cyber threats and vulnerabilities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an implementation duty: deploy and maintain risk-proportionate security controls, potentially including encryption, to reduce incident impacts. Norm B is a risk-identification and assessment duty: maintain an inventory of ICT-risk sources and evaluate threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios. Identifying and assessing risks is not substantially the same practical action as implementing security measures to control them.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms have a related risk-management objective and ongoing trigger, but impose materially different compliance actions—risk assessment and identification versus implementation of protective security measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulatory action following a legally relevant event and involve an entity subject to the relevant regime, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require communicating information about a data/security incident to a public authority, including information enabling assessment or mitigation of its consequences.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling or communicating information about ICT/data incidents following an incident-related trigger.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to promptly notify the affected data subject of a high-risk personal-data breach, subject to specified exceptions or substitute public communication. Norm B, as extracted, preserves financial entities' responsibility for handling reported ICT incidents and describes optional supervisory feedback; it does not require the financial entity to notify affected persons.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is substantively different: mandatory prompt notification to affected individuals versus continued responsibility for incident handling and consequences, with supervisory feedback being discretionary.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require documenting information about adverse events/incidents, including consequences and corrective or remedial measures, so that the relevant authority can oversee or respond to them.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to document all personal-data breaches, including breach facts, consequences, and measures taken, primarily to enable supervisory compliance checks. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep, document, and promptly report relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to the AI Office and, where applicable, national authorities. Thus B adds retention and an urgent reporting duty, concerns a narrower incident category, and has different recipients and regulatory context.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share incident-related documentation, but the required compliance action is materially different because Norm B includes an express, immediate reporting obligation to specified authorities, whereas Norm A requires documentation only and does not itself require reporting.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to implement and maintain measures or controls addressing ICT/network security risks and limiting the effects of incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a broad security-risk management duty on providers of public electronic communications networks or services, focused on risks to network/service security and consequences for national security or public order. Norm B imposes a substantially more specific ICT-risk-management and incident-handling framework on certain financial entities, including rapid identification and detection of ICT-risk sources and anomalies and rapid handling of ICT incidents, alongside extensive governance, continuity, testing, and data-protection requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations overlap at a high level but differ in substantive scope, regulated sectors, and required operational content: B mandates a documented, continuously monitored and tested ICT-risk framework with detection and incident-response capabilities, whereas A requires taking prescribed technical, operational, and organisational security measures to control network/service-security risks and mitigate specified public consequences.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible entity to report a qualifying security/data incident to a public supervisory or incident-response authority without undue delay and, where necessary, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires reporting to both the CSIRT and the competent authority and includes specified incident information, including an initial assessment, compromise indicators, and information about cross-border effects. verdict.evidence_span_b: Centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen verrichten kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen voordat nieuwe of bestaande toepassingen en infrastructuurcomponenten, en ICT-diensten ter ondersteuning van kritieke of belangrijke functies van de financiële entiteit worden ingezet of opnieuw worden ingezet.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het omgaan met ICT-/cyberincidenten en communicatie daarover, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verplicht het centrale contactpunt tot een periodieke, geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde rapportage aan Enisa over reeds gemelde incidenten en dreigingen. Norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten vooraf over crisiscommunicatieplannen te beschikken waarmee zij ernstige ICT-incidenten of kwetsbaarheden verantwoord kunnen bekendmaken aan cliënten, tegenpartijen en eventueel het publiek.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste handeling, ontvanger en timing verschillen materieel: periodieke samenvattende rapportage aan Enisa versus het beschikbaar hebben van een crisiscommunicatieplan voor externe bekendmaking aan betrokkenen of het publiek.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to an event or situation involving ICT/AI-related risk by requiring organizational action, but they do not require the same practical compliance measure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the financial entity’s governing body to establish internal reporting channels enabling it to obtain information about ICT third-party-provider arrangements, planned material changes, and their effects. Norm B requires the provider or potential provider to report each serious incident during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority and to take immediate mitigation, suspension, termination, and recall-procedure measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions and recipients differ substantially: internal governance and information-gathering channels versus external incident notification and immediate risk-control/testing measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a regulated entity to carry out a specified compliance activity following a cybersecurity-related trigger or framework: A requires submitting a formal incident final report, while B requires conducting ICT security and resilience tests.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty: the entity must submit a detailed final (or, where applicable, interim) report to its CSIRT and competent authority within the prescribed period. Norm B is an operational testing duty: the relevant testing programme must provide for and implement various ICT vulnerability, security, resilience, and performance tests. Reporting an incident and testing ICT systems are substantively different actions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: mandatory submission of an incident report to authorities versus execution of ICT tests.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen
verdict.evidence_span_b: voorziet, overeenkomstig de criteria in artikel 4, lid 2, in de uitvoering van passende tests

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het reageren op of afhandelen van meldingen/transactiemeldingen na een relevante gebeurtenis, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist dat datarapporteringsdienstaanbieders systemen beschikbaar hebben die transactiemeldingen op volledigheid controleren, omissies en evidente fouten detecteren en hertransmissie kunnen verzoeken. Norm B vereist daarentegen dat een ernstig incident met een hoog-risico-AI-systeem daadwerkelijk wordt gemeld, met een specifieke onmiddellijke en uiterlijke termijn van tien dagen bij overlijden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste handeling verschilt materieel: technische detectie- en validatiecapaciteit voor transactiemeldingen versus het indienen van een incidentmelding binnen een wettelijke termijn.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken
verdict.evidence_span_b: de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern handling information about ICT/cyber incidents reported under the NIS2/DORA framework, but they do not require the same operational act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the central contact point to submit a recurring, anonymised and aggregated summary report to ENISA every three months. Norm B concerns the competent authority acknowledging receipt and optionally giving feedback or guidance to a financial entity, while stating that the financial entity remains responsible for handling the incidents and their consequences; it does not impose a periodic summary-reporting duty to ENISA.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action, recipient, and procedure differ materially: periodic aggregation and transmission of incident data to ENISA versus supervisory feedback/responsibility concerning reported incidents.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address measures taken in response to security or personal-data incidents to reduce harm to affected persons or services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an ongoing, risk-based duty on public electronic communications providers to implement appropriate technical, operational, and organisational security measures, potentially including encryption, to manage service-security risks and minimise incident effects. Norm B imposes a conditional, incident-triggered communication duty on a controller: promptly notify the data subject of a personal-data breach likely to create a high risk, subject to the stated exceptions. Implementing security measures is not substantially the same practical action as notifying affected individuals.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: preventive/ongoing security-risk management versus prompt breach notification to data subjects.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen, waaronder in voorkomend geval versleuteling
verdict.evidence_span_b: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op handelingen die verband houden met ICT-compliance, maar zij verplichten niet tot dezelfde concrete actie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verplicht tot periodieke en incident-triggered documentatie en evaluatie van het ICT-risicobeheerkader, met indiening van het evaluatieverslag op verzoek. Norm B verplicht bepaalde financiële entiteiten om ICT-incidentmeldingen (waaronder vrijwillige meldingen) ook aan een aangewezen sectoraal CSIRT te doen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste handeling verschilt materieel: periodieke evaluatie/documentatie van een intern risicobeheerkader versus externe melding van ICT-incidenten aan een CSIRT.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require action in response to ICT-related risk or incidents, but their operative compliance duties are not the same: Norm A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident externally to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours, whereas Norm B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be periodically and incident-triggeredly documented and evaluated, with an evaluation report submitted on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external incident-notification duty with a fixed 24-hour deadline and a specified recipient; Norm B is an internal governance/documentation and evaluation duty, with no fixed deadline or specified recipient in the extracted provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different operative action, recipient, and timing: incident reporting to a public body versus periodic/incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting a qualifying incident to a public authority: significant incidents under NIS2 are reported to the CSIRT or competent authority, while serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems are reported to the relevant market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ materially in scope and procedure. Norm A concerns trust-service providers and requires reporting significant incidents affecting trust services within 24 hours, as part of a broader staged reporting regime. Norm B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems and requires reporting serious incidents to the market-surveillance authority where the incident occurred, generally immediately after causation is established and no later than 15 days after awareness, or within two days for specified widespread or particularly serious incidents; it also entails a subsequent investigation and cooperation duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared act of incident notification is not the same substantive compliance obligation because the regulated sectors, incident categories, reporting recipients, triggering conditions, deadlines, and surrounding procedural duties materially differ.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met gevolgen van ICT-/gegevensverwerkingsincidenten, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliance-actie op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A legt een aansprakelijkheids- en schadevergoedingsverplichting op na onrechtmatige verwerking; norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten tot post-incidentanalyse en, op verzoek, het meedelen van aangebrachte verbeteringen aan de bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste handeling verschilt wezenlijk: juridische aansprakelijkheid voor veroorzaakte schade versus evalueren, verbeteringen identificeren en daarover rapporteren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require action following a personal-data breach, but they do not require the same notification in practice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the provider to notify the affected data subject, whereas Norm B requires the controller to report the breach to the competent supervisory authority. The recipients, and therefore the compliance procedures and purposes, are different; Norm B also specifies a possible 72-hour deadline and a delay justification.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different mandatory recipient and compliance channel: individual data-subject notification versus supervisory-authority breach reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt notification/reporting after a serious or significant incident, but the required recipient and reporting function differ.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to inform its own service recipients (customers/users) about significant incidents affecting service provision. Norm B requires high-risk AI providers or deployers to report serious incidents to Member State market-surveillance authorities, with specified deadlines and special shorter deadlines for widespread breaches or deaths.
verdict.criterion_fired: The addressee and substantive compliance purpose differ: customer/service-user notification versus regulatory incident reporting to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in the context of regulated digital technology and require the addressee to take a compliance-related action concerning technology-related risks or impacts.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a substantive, ongoing technical and organisational prevention duty: financial entities must use ICT solutions and processes that prevent availability failures, loss or compromise of data, and confidentiality breaches. Norm B imposes a procedural reporting duty: after conducting a fundamental-rights impact assessment, the deployer must notify the market surveillance authority of the results and submit a completed template.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: preventive ICT risk controls versus notification and submission of an assessment template.
verdict.evidence_span_a: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het omgaan met informatie over digitale/AI-risico’s, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist dat financiële entiteiten blijvend beschikken over capaciteiten en personeel om kwetsbaarheden, dreigingen en incidenten te verzamelen en de gevolgen daarvan te analyseren. Norm B vereist dat een gebruiksverantwoordelijke, nadat een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem is uitgevoerd, de resultaten aan de markttoezichtautoriteit meldt en een ingevuld sjabloon indient.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste handeling, het doel en de geadresseerde verschillen wezenlijk: interne operationele weerbaarheids- en analysecapaciteit versus externe kennisgeving van een specifieke grondrechtenbeoordeling met formulier.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen, en om de waarschijnlijke gevolgen ervan voor hun digitale operationele weerbaarheid te analyseren
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern consequences following a legally relevant incident or infringement, but they do not require the same compliance action in practice.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to proactively send an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, including specified information. Norm B grants an injured person a right to receive compensation from a controller or processor; it does not impose an incident-reporting duty on the addressee.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative actions, direction of conduct, and beneficiaries differ substantially: mandatory regulatory notification versus payment/receipt of damages compensation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting a qualifying incident to a competent authority under the applicable incident-reporting regime.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a general duty on essential or important entities to report every significant incident in accordance with Articles 26–29. Norm B concerns a narrower class of high-risk AI systems that are medical-device safety components or devices, limits reportable incidents to a specified category, and requires reporting to the designated national authority in the Member State where the incident occurred. The norms therefore differ in scope, qualifying incident, and specified recipient, even though both involve incident reporting.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is not substantially identical because the norms impose materially different reporting scopes and recipient rules: general reporting of every significant incident under Articles 26–29 versus restricted reporting of specified serious incidents to the designated authority where the incident occurred.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating incident-related information to competent public authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires, upon request, a specific estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents. Norm B requires providers to maintain and document information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures and to report it without delay, including to the AI Office and potentially national authorities. The reporting duties differ in subject matter, trigger, timing, and scope.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: an on-request cost/loss estimate versus proactive, immediate incident and remediation-information recordkeeping and reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op het vastleggen of meedelen van informatie over een relevante gebeurtenis aan een bevoegde overheidsinstantie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke tot interne documentatie van alle persoonsgegevensinbreuken, inclusief feiten, gevolgen en corrigerende maatregelen, zodat toezicht op naleving mogelijk is. Norm B verplicht de gebruiksverantwoordelijke daarentegen tot een externe kennisgeving aan de markttoezichtautoriteit van de resultaten van een voorafgaande grondrechteneffectbeoordeling, met indiening van een ingevuld sjabloon; het gaat dus om een formele melding van beoordelingsresultaten, niet om incidentdocumentatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De concrete compliance-acties verschillen wezenlijk: documenteren en beschikbaar houden voor toezicht versus actief kennisgeven aan een markttoezichtautoriteit en een voorgeschreven formulier indienen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met informatie over ICT-/elektronische-dienstverlening en richten zich op organisatorische beheersing van digitale risico’s, maar zij vereisen niet dezelfde concrete handeling.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verplicht het bestuursorgaan of de aangewezen organisatie om de minister onverwijld te informeren over een beveiligings- of integriteitsinbreuk of misbruik van toegang, inclusief alle benodigde informatie. Norm B verplicht het leidinggevend orgaan om interne meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau op te zetten waarmee informatie over ICT-dienstverleningsregelingen, geplande materiële wijzigingen en de gevolgen daarvan kan worden ingewonnen. Dat is een structurele governance- en informatie-inwinningsmaatregel, geen incidentmelding aan een overheidsinstantie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste compliance-acties verschillen substantieel: externe, onverwijlde melding van een concreet beveiligingsincident of misbruik aan Onze Minister versus het permanent inrichten van interne bedrijfsbrede meldingskanalen voor governance-informatie over ICT-dienstverleners en wijzigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in the context of a serious incident and require the addressee to take a compliance-related action, but the actions are not substantially the same: Norm A requires periodic and incident-related documentation and evaluation of the ICT risk-management framework, whereas Norm B requires an immediate investigation of the serious incident and the relevant AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns documenting and evaluating an organisation-wide ICT risk-management framework, including periodically and when serious ICT-related incidents occur. Norm B concerns conducting an immediate, incident-specific investigation of the serious incident and AI system, with risk assessment and corrective measures, plus cooperation with authorities and restrictions on altering the system before causal evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: framework documentation/evaluation versus an urgent incident investigation with risk assessment and corrective action.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations triggered by an ICT/data-related incident, but their required compliance actions are not the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires prompt notification of the affected data subject about a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy. Norm B requires financial entities, during ICT-incident recovery or data reconstruction, to perform controls and reconciliations ensuring the highest level of data integrity and consistency across systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative actions, recipients, and compliance purposes differ substantially: individual breach notification versus internal recovery-stage data-integrity controls.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information to a competent authority concerning incident-related matters.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to proactively report a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority, within 24 hours (and with specified incident information under the referenced paragraph). Norm B requires other financial entities, only upon request, to provide competent authorities with an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents. The required content, triggering procedure, and practical compliance action therefore differ substantially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations require materially different acts: proactive incident notification versus on-request submission of an annual cost-and-loss estimate.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms relate broadly to responding to or managing technology-related risks/incidents, but they do not require the same operational action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to deploy sufficient resources and capabilities for ongoing monitoring and detection of user activity, ICT anomalies, and ICT-related incidents. Norm B requires reporting each serious incident found during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority, plus immediate mitigation, suspension or termination of testing, and a recall procedure.

verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance acts differ in substantive purpose and content: urgent incident reporting versus applying for designation as a conformity-assessment body.

Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test detection mechanisms for anomalous activity, ICT-network performance issues, ICT incidents, and physical single points of failure.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires post-incident review of causes, procedures, effectiveness, and needed improvements; Norm B requires reporting the incident to market-surveillance authorities within a specified deadline.

Norm B is a standing preparedness and communication-planning obligation aimed at informing private stakeholders and possibly the public; it does not require filing the incident with authorities.

verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to adverse ICT/security events, but their required compliance actions are not the same: Norm A requires providers to implement ongoing, risk-based technical, operational, and organizational security measures, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to notify affected clients promptly about a serious ICT incident and mitigation measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive and continuing security-risk-management obligation concerning the provider’s services and networks. Norm B is an event-triggered, client-facing notification obligation, including specified information and an urgent timing requirement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in their operative action and compliance object: implementation of security controls versus prompt notification of clients.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het omgaan met ICT/cyberrisico’s, maar zij vereisen niet dezelfde concrete compliancehandeling.

Norm B requires reporting specified serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI/device systems to the designated national authority in the Member State where the incident occurred, with no deadline stated in the provision.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to take a cybersecurity-related compliance measure concerning risks to networked or AI-related systems.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to exclusively use products or services from suppliers other than a minister-designated risky party, potentially replacing or ending existing products or services within a minister-set period. Norm B requires providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models to evaluate and mitigate systemic risks, document and promptly report serious incidents and corrective measures to authorities, and ensure cybersecurity protection. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant provider/entity to report a serious or significant incident to a public authority (and, under Norm A, also to its CSIRT).

Norm B concerns serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems and requires reporting to the market-surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred, with different causation-based and 15-day/two-day deadlines and subsequent investigation duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The reporting action is not substantially the same in practice because the regulated incident, reporting recipients, territorial allocation, timing framework, and accompanying compliance procedure differ in substance.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a compliance measure in response to ICT-related operational risk or incidents, but that shared subject matter and triggering context do not make the required actions substantially identical.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/digital compliance, but they do not require the same operational act. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security incidents and involve communication or regulatory handling after an incident, but they do not require the same practical action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an urgent, affirmative duty on a public body or designated organisation to notify the Minister and provide all necessary information. Norm B concerns the competent authority acknowledging receipt and optionally providing feedback, while leaving the financial entity responsible for handling the incident and its consequences; it does not impose an equivalent notification duty on the financial entity in the quoted provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: mandatory immediate incident notification and information provision versus supervisory acknowledgment/optional feedback and continued responsibility for incident handling.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in connection with an ICT/significant incident and require the regulated entity to take a compliance-related action, but the actions are materially different.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an urgent external notification (an early warning) to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, with specified information. Norm B requires internal recovery-stage controls and reconciliations to preserve data integrity and consistency when restoring or reconstructing data; it does not require notifying an authority or CSIRT.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: incident reporting to designated public/response bodies versus operational data-integrity controls during ICT-incident recovery.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to ICT/data incidents, but their required compliance actions are not substantially the same: Norm A requires prompt notification by a processor to the controller after becoming aware of a personal-data breach, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to design, establish, and implement an ongoing ICT-incident management process covering detection, classification, responsibilities, communications, escalation, and response.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered, bilateral notification duty directed to a specific recipient; Norm B is an organizational governance and operational-process duty, including establishing and implementing procedures for managing ICT incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in their core action and practical compliance object: incident notification to a controller versus creation and implementation of a comprehensive incident-management process.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an organizational measure concerning cybersecurity-related information: Norm A requires the central contact point to submit a periodic, anonymized and aggregated report to ENISA, while Norm B requires financial entities to deploy resources and capabilities for ongoing monitoring and detection.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a specific quarterly reporting and information-transmission obligation imposed on a central contact point; Norm B is an operational cybersecurity-monitoring obligation imposed on financial entities, involving surveillance of user activity and ICT anomalies/incidents rather than submission of reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: periodic reporting to ENISA versus deploying monitoring and detection capabilities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to establish and operate an incident-related governance or management process that includes handling incident information and responding to incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a comprehensive ICT-incident management process covering detection, management, reporting, classification, responsibilities, communications, escalation, and recovery. Norm B requires providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models specifically to retain, document, and promptly report information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures, alongside separate model-evaluation, systemic-risk mitigation, and cybersecurity duties. The reporting/recordkeeping component overlaps, but the overall compliance obligations and operational scope differ substantially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose substantially the same practical action: A mandates implementation of an end-to-end ICT-incident management process, whereas B mandates incident-information recordkeeping, documentation, and prompt reporting as one element of a broader AI-model risk regime.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to report information about a qualifying adverse event to a public authority promptly.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to notify the competent data-protection supervisory authority of a personal-data breach, subject to a risk-based exception, generally within 72 hours of becoming aware and with reasons for delay. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep and document relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures, and report it without delay to the AI Office and, where appropriate, national competent authorities. B therefore adds an ongoing recordkeeping/documentation duty, covers serious incidents and corrective measures rather than personal-data breaches, and has different recipients and timing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The reporting components are not substantially the same in practice because the triggering events, information-handling duties, recipients, and timing framework materially differ; Norm B includes a distinct recordkeeping/documentation obligation in addition to urgent reporting.

verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting a qualifying adverse event or incident to a designated public authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a public electronic communications service provider to notify the Dutch data-protection authority without delay of a security breach affecting personal-data protection. Norm B concerns serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems and requires reporting them to the designated national authority in the Member State where the incident occurred; it also limits the reportable incidents to the specified category in Article 3(49)(c). The reporting duties therefore differ in regulated subject matter, triggering conditions, recipient, and territorial/procedural scope.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is not substantially the same because the norms impose distinct incident-reporting regimes with different qualifying events, authorities, and scope.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist dat bepaalde financiële entiteiten operationele lessen uit tests en incidentanalyses opnemen in hun ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt communication to another party after becoming aware of, or in connection with, a potentially relevant cyber/data-security event.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires informing potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and where necessary informing them of the threat itself. Norm B requires a processor to notify the controller that a personal-data breach has occurred; it does not require advice on protective measures or notification of service recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required communication's recipient and substantive content differ: actionable threat-response guidance to potentially affected service recipients versus breach notification to the controller.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an institutional actor to provide information to another oversight/compliance-related body upon request or in specified circumstances.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to make available their ICT-services information register (or parts of it), plus any information needed for effective supervision, to the competent authority on request. Norm B requires notified bodies to proactively share relevant information about negative conformity-assessment results with peer notified bodies, and to share positive results only upon request. The recipients, information, and disclosure purpose therefore differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required disclosure is substantively different: different sender and recipient relationships, different information subject matter, and different triggering rules (supervisory request versus mandatory peer notification for negative results, with request-based disclosure only for positive results).

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about a significant incident or personal-data breach to designated public authorities, and in A also to the relevant CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to submit an incident notification, with a special 24-hour deadline for a trust-service provider and the fuller incident-information content supplied by the referenced paragraph. Norm B specifies the substantive contents of a notification to the data-protection authority and affected person, including the breach's nature, information sources, recommended mitigation measures, and— for the authority—effects and response measures. It does not itself impose the incident-reporting action or deadline stated in A.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: A is a prompt incident-reporting obligation to a CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B is a content requirement for notifications to the data-protection authority and affected individual, with additional authority-specific information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern a response following a triggering event involving a regulated entity, but they do not require the same practical compliance action. Norm A requires the affected entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, with specified incident information and a 24-hour deadline. Norm B requires the lead overseer to impose a coercive daily fine on a critical ICT third-party provider, for up to six months or until the underlying obligations are fulfilled.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty imposed on an essential or important entity offering a trust service; Norm B is an enforcement power/duty involving the imposition of a daily coercive fine by the lead overseer on a critical ICT third-party provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions, responsible actors, recipients, and legal functions differ substantially: reporting an incident versus imposing an enforcement fine.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a report to be submitted following an incident-related triggering event. However, Norm A requires the regulated entity to submit a substantive progress report instead of a final report when the incident is ongoing, followed by a final report within one month after resolution; Norm B requires reporting a serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority under Article 73.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns staged incident reporting by an essential or important entity to its CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident details and a post-resolution deadline. Norm B concerns notification of a serious incident occurring during real-world AI testing to the national market-surveillance authority, alongside separate immediate risk-mitigation, suspension/termination, and recall-procedure duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The reporting actions differ materially in recipient, report type, timing, and procedural context: A is a progress/final incident-reporting regime, while B is a serious-incident notification obligation during AI testing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by a security-related event or risk and concern an entity within the digital/electronic-communications sphere, but their required compliance actions are materially different: Norm A requires an entity to use only products or services from permitted suppliers, potentially replacing or ending use of specified existing products or services; Norm B requires a communications-service provider to notify the Dutch data-protection authority promptly of a qualifying security breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a procurement/use restriction and, where applicable, supplier or product/service replacement or termination. Norm B imposes an immediate incident-reporting obligation to a regulator.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: exclusive use of non-designated suppliers versus prompt notification of a qualifying security breach.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to continuously identify ICT-risk sources and assess relevant cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios. Norm B requires providers or deployers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to national market-surveillance authorities within a specified deadline.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires providers to implement technical, operational, and organisational security measures to manage network or service security risks and limit incident consequences. verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the public electronic communications service provider to maintain an ongoing register or overview of all personal-data breaches, including specified facts and information. Norm B requires a processor to notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach. Record-keeping and breach notification are distinct obligations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: maintaining a breach register versus promptly informing another party of the breach.
