Norm B vereist het opnemen van operationele conclusies uit ICT-tests en incidentanalyses in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces, als onderdeel van een veel breder ICT-risicobeheerkader. Dat is geen verplichting om een register van persoonsgegevensinbreuken bij te houden.
verdict.criterion_fired: De concrete compliance-acties verschillen materieel: een incidentenoverzicht bijhouden versus test- en incidentconclusies integreren in een risicobeoordelingsproces.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to ICT/data incidents, but their required compliance actions are not substantially the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to promptly notify the affected data subject of a personal-data breach when it likely creates a high risk, subject to the stated exceptions. Norm B requires financial entities to classify ICT-related incidents and assess their effects using specified criteria; it does not require notifying affected persons.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative actions differ in substance: individual breach notification versus internal incident classification and impact assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten classificeren ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en bepalen de effecten daarvan op basis van de volgende criteria

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information about an event or circumstance to a public authority, but they do not require the same operational act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires broad, on-request and proactive provision of whatever data and information the Minister needs to prevent or end infringements affecting secure and reliable electronic access. Norm B requires reporting defined serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems to the designated national authority in the Member State where the incident occurred.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in scope, trigger, content, and recipient: an ongoing/proactive information-supply duty to a Minister versus a specific serious-incident notification duty to a territorially designated national authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responses to technology-related risks or incidents, but they do not require the same concrete compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires maintaining capabilities and personnel to collect and analyze information about vulnerabilities, cyber threats, and ICT incidents as part of ongoing digital operational resilience. Norm B requires high-risk AI providers (and, where applicable, deployers) to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities within specified deadlines, including shorter deadlines for widespread incidents or deaths.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required actions differ substantively: continuous internal information-gathering and analytical capacity versus an external regulatory notification triggered by a serious incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen, en om de waarschijnlijke gevolgen ervan voor hun digitale operationele weerbaarheid te analyseren
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het reageren op incidenten en het verstrekken van informatie aan een bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist het documenteren en bewaren van een intern dossier over alle persoonsgegevensinbreuken, met feiten, gevolgen en corrigerende maatregelen, zodat toezicht mogelijk is. Norm B vereist daarentegen een externe melding van ernstige AI-incidenten aan markttoezichtautoriteiten, onmiddellijk en binnen toepasselijke termijnen (in beginsel uiterlijk 15 dagen, met kortere termijnen voor bepaalde ernstige gevallen).
verdict.criterion_fired: De feitelijke compliance-acties verschillen wezenlijk: interne documentatie van alle inbreuken versus tijdige externe incidentmelding aan een markttoezichtautoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen verplichten een aangewezen entiteit om informatie over een voorafgaande beoordeling of gebeurtenis aan een bevoegde overheidsinstantie te melden, met gebruikmaking van voorgeschreven informatie/formulieren.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft de doorlopende, gefaseerde melding van ernstige ICT-incidenten (eerste kennisgeving, tussentijdse updates en eindverslag) door financiële entiteiten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit. Norm B betreft een eenmalige kennisgeving van de resultaten van een voorafgaande grondrechteneffectbeoordeling van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem, inclusief een ingevuld sjabloon, door de gebruiksverantwoordelijke aan de markttoezichtautoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: De concrete compliance-actie verschilt materieel: incidentrapportage en opvolgende status-/eindrapporten tegenover melding van beoordelingsresultaten met een ingevuld formulier. Het gedeelde element — informatie aan een autoriteit verstrekken — is slechts een generieke meldingsvorm.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to implement or maintain measures addressing ICT/network security risks and their consequences.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires public electronic communications providers to take prescribed technical, operational, and organisational security-risk measures aimed at limiting the effects of security incidents on national security or public order. Norm B, for specified small or exempt financial entities, requires a documented ICT-risk-management framework and a broad set of operational controls, including monitoring, resilience, incident detection and response, continuity, testing, and incorporation of lessons learned into risk assessment. Norm B's specific extracted action is the latter feedback/integration duty, not merely taking security measures generally.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is substantively different: Norm A is a general security-risk mitigation obligation for communications networks/services, whereas Norm B imposes a specific ICT-governance and continuous risk-management control, including feeding test and post-incident conclusions into the ICT-risk assessment process.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen, teneinde de gevolgen van beveiligingsincidenten op de nationale veiligheid of openbare orde te beperken
verdict.evidence_span_b: de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern consequences following a legally relevant event involving a regulated entity, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a proactive reporting duty: the entity must notify each significant incident in accordance with Articles 26–29. Norm B establishes civil liability for damage caused by unlawful processing (with processor-specific conditions); it does not require incident reporting or another comparable operational notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative actions differ in substance: mandatory incident notification versus liability to compensate for damage caused by non-compliant processing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke die bij verwerking is betrokken, is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address the handling of ICT/AI-related risks or incidents by regulated entities, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test detection mechanisms for anomalous activities, ICT performance issues, ICT incidents, and physical single points of failure. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep and document information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures and report it without delay to specified authorities. The former is an ongoing detection capability; the latter is incident recordkeeping and regulatory reporting.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required operational acts and outputs differ materially: detection-system implementation and testing versus documentation and prompt reporting of serious incidents and corrective measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren, met inbegrip van kwesties op het gebied van ICT-netwerkprestaties en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, en om potentiële zwakke fysieke punten (“single points of failure”) te identificeren
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to promptly notify another designated party after becoming aware of a security or personal-data breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a public body or designated organization to notify the Minister about breaches affecting its own electronic service or misuse/unauthorized use of access, and to provide all necessary information. Norm B requires a processor to notify the controller, without unreasonable delay, upon becoming aware of a personal-data breach. The recipient, regulated relationship, triggering breach, and scope of the notification duty therefore differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required notification is directed to a different recipient and concerns a materially different regulated relationship and subject matter; the shared promptness and breach-notification structure do not make the substantive compliance action the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening
verdict.evidence_span_b: informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulatory compliance following a legally relevant event and may involve oversight by a supervisory authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to document personal-data breaches, including facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so the authority can verify compliance. Norm B concerns the lead overseer imposing a coercive fine daily on a critical ICT third-party service provider until obligations are fulfilled, for up to six months; it is an enforcement sanction, not a documentation duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world actions differ substantially: record-keeping and preservation of breach information versus imposition of a daily coercive penalty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action following an ICT-related incident and involve communicating information to another party, but they require different substantive measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires prompt notification of service recipients about significant incidents that may adversely affect service provision. Norm B requires financial entities, upon request, to report to competent authorities the changes implemented after post-incident evaluations; it also entails conducting those evaluations, analyzing causes, and identifying improvements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required communication, recipient, content, and triggering/procedural conditions differ materially: service-user incident notification versus authority-facing reporting of post-evaluation changes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance activities triggered in the context of operational or serious incidents/risks and involve regulated entities taking a prescribed action, but the actual actions are different.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires carrying out a structured programme of ICT resilience and security tests, including vulnerability assessments, scans, penetration tests, and other technical or organisational testing. Norm B requires submitting a notification of a serious incident, with an immediate trigger upon establishing or suspecting causation and an outer deadline of ten days in the case of death.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: testing ICT systems versus reporting a serious AI incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: in de uitvoering van passende tests, zoals kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen en -scans, opensourceanalyses, netwerkbeveiligingsbeoordelingen, kloofanalyses, beoordelingen van fysieke beveiliging, vragenlijsten en scanningsoftwareoplossingen, beoordelingen van broncodes indien mogelijk, scenariogebaseerde tests, compatibiliteitstests, prestatietests, eind-tot-eindtests en penetratietests
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern reporting an incident to a competent public authority following a serious or otherwise reportable incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to submit a detailed final report (or, while the incident continues, a progress report followed by a final report) to both its CSIRT and competent authority, with specified substantive information and deadlines. Norm B requires reporting the incident itself to the designated national competent authority, with no comparable final-report contents, CSIRT recipient, or stated deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance deliverable and procedure differ materially: a structured, information-rich final/progress reporting duty to two bodies versus a basic incident notification to one designated national authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational handling of ICT/security incidents, but they do not require the same concrete act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a trust-service provider to externally report a significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours of becoming aware of it. Norm B requires a financial entity to internally register all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats, and to establish processes for monitoring, handling, follow-up, and remediation; it does not impose the same 24-hour external notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: external regulatory incident notification versus internal incident registration and management processes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen. Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to communicate incident information to an external recipient without undue delay or through prescribed incident-reporting procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires notifying the entity’s service recipients—customers or users—of significant incidents that may adversely affect service provision. Norm B requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, including structured initial, interim, and final reports under the referenced procedure. The recipients, purpose, and reporting content are materially different.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in recipient and substantive compliance purpose: customer/service-user notification versus regulatory incident reporting to a competent authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to provide information to a public authority in connection with a serious/significant ICT incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity, in an early warning, to state whether the incident was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act (and, under the provision, also to state possible cross-border effects and provide the responsible officer’s contact details). Norm B requires non-micro financial entities, upon request, to provide competent authorities with an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses resulting from serious ICT-related incidents. These are different information disclosures with different substantive content and triggering procedures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required information and practical compliance action differ in substance: incident-cause/cross-border-effect/contact disclosure in an early warning versus a requested financial-loss estimate.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address cybersecurity-related protection or response, but they do not require the same practical compliance action. Norm A requires an entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and where necessary to notify them of the threat itself. Norm B requires financial entities to deploy suitable ICT technologies and processes that prevent or mitigate specified data-security failures, including loss of availability, compromised authenticity or integrity, confidentiality breaches, and data loss.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent external communication and guidance duty toward service recipients; Norm B is an ongoing technical and organizational preventive-control duty concerning ICT systems and data protection.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: notification and advice to recipients versus implementation and operation of preventive ICT safeguards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responses to ICT-related risk or incidents, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to send an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, promptly or within 24 hours, including specified information. Norm B requires the management body to establish and oversee governance arrangements, including enterprise-level reporting channels for obtaining information about ICT-service-provider arrangements and changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative acts, recipients, and compliance outputs differ substantially: incident notification to public/response authorities versus establishment and governance of internal organizational reporting channels and ICT-risk controls.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose a mandatory action on regulated entities triggered in the context of digital/cyber compliance: the entity must take a specified administrative/compliance step.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to register all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and to establish incident-monitoring, treatment, and follow-up procedures. Norm B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the competent notifying authority. These are substantively different actions: ongoing incident recording and process establishment versus filing an application for official notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions, objects, and practical outcomes differ in substance, despite both being mandatory administrative obligations for entities in the digital-law domain.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op optreden naar aanleiding van ICT/AI-risico’s of incidenten en vereisen snelle actie door de aanbieder of entiteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist een doorlopende preventieve en organisatorische ICT-risicobeheerfunctie: bronnen van risico’s en anomalieën zo spoedig mogelijk identificeren en detecteren en incidenten snel afhandelen. Norm B vereist daarentegen, nadat een ernstig incident is gemeld, een onverwijld, specifiek onderzoek naar dat incident en het betrokken AI-systeem, inclusief risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen, met samenwerking met autoriteiten en beperkingen op het wijzigen van het systeem tijdens het onderzoek.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie verschilt substantieel: voortdurende detectie en snelle incidentafhandeling versus een ex-post formeel onderzoek met risicobeoordeling en corrigerende maatregelen na melding van een ernstig incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: ervoor zorgen dat bronnen van ICT-risico’s en anomalieën in de netwerk- en informatiesystemen zo spoedig mogelijk worden geïdentificeerd en gedetecteerd en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten snel kunnen worden afgehandeld
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by a significant/serious ICT incident and require a communication or notification related to that incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the essential or important entity to report every significant incident under the detailed procedures in Articles 26–29, apparently to the competent authority or other designated recipient. Norm B requires a financial entity to notify its potentially affected clients directly and without delay, including the incident and mitigation measures; its second paragraph also concerns protective measures for clients facing a significant cyber threat.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required recipient and substantive communication differ: regulatory incident reporting under Norm A versus direct client notification and mitigation information under Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to another party in connection with an ICT-related event or post-event process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires urgent proactive communication to potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and possibly notice of the threat itself. Norm B requires financial entities, other than micro-enterprises, to provide competent authorities—only upon request—with information about changes implemented after post-incident evaluations. The recipients, information conveyed, triggering conditions, and proactive versus request-based nature differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: threat-response guidance to potentially affected service recipients versus post-incident change reporting to competent authorities on request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to submit a formal filing to a designated public authority. In practice, each involves initiating an administrative submission procedure with an authority, rather than merely notifying an informal contact.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an urgent incident report to both the CSIRT and competent authority, with a 24-hour fallback deadline and the substantive incident information described in the referenced paragraph. Norm B requires a conformity-assessment body to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority, with no stated deadline or incident-reporting content. The filings serve different regulatory purposes and contain materially different information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required submissions differ in substantive purpose, content, recipients, and timing: incident notification and assessment versus an application for designation/notification as a conformity-assessment body.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern the protection of personal/data-related information by regulated entities, but they do not require the same operational measure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires maintaining a register or overview of all personal-data breaches, including specified facts and information. Norm B requires using suitable ICT technologies and processes to prevent or mitigate data-security failures, including loss of availability, compromised authenticity or integrity, confidentiality breaches, and data loss.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A specifically concerns significant incidents affecting trust services and requires reporting within 24 hours of awareness, while Norm B concerns serious ICT-related incidents of financial entities and requires a staged first, interim, and final reporting process within deadlines set under Article 20. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in the context of a regulated incident or processing-related event and concern the regulated entity’s legal consequences or follow-up obligations.

verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is substantively different: mandatory regulatory reporting with prescribed contents and timing versus liability for compensatory damages.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take a specified operational action in response to an ICT/significant incident: Norm A requires reporting the incident to designated authorities, while Norm B requires performing controls during incident recovery to preserve data integrity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The obligations differ substantively. Norm A is an incident-notification duty directed externally to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, with a 24-hour (or immediate) deadline and specified reporting content by reference to paragraph 1. Norm B is an internal recovery and data-integrity control duty, including reconciliations and checks when restoring or reconstructing data; it is not a reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action, recipient, and practical purpose are materially different: external incident notification versus internal recovery/data-integrity verification.

In practice, each involves making an incident report to a CSIRT, although Norm A also requires reporting to the competent authority and includes specified accompanying information.

Norm B extends specified EU-regulation incident reports—including voluntary reports—by requiring them also to be submitted to the sector-designated CSIRT; it does not itself set a deadline or add the same information requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared act of reporting an incident to a CSIRT is not the whole compliance obligation: the norms differ materially in scope, reporting basis, recipients, timing, and required contents. Norm B is an additional routing requirement for reports under the EU regulation, whereas Norm A is a standalone, time-bound significant-incident notification duty to two authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take action in response to ICT/data-security risk, but their operative compliance duties are not the same: Norm A requires prompt notification of affected data subjects about a high-risk personal-data breach, subject to the stated exceptions; Norm B requires ongoing ICT-risk identification and assessment, including annual risk-scenario evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered external communication duty directed to data subjects. Norm B is a continuous internal risk-management and assessment duty concerning ICT risks, threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios; it does not require notifying affected individuals.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world compliance actions differ in substance: breach notification to individuals versus permanent and periodic ICT-risk identification and assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible party to promptly report a security-related incident or misuse event to a public authority, including the applicable incident information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a bestuursorgaan or designated organization to notify the Minister immediately of a breach or misuse involving its own electronic service and to provide all necessary information. Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems (and, where applicable, deployers) to report serious incidents to the relevant Member State market-surveillance authorities, with the fuller procedure requiring reporting after a causal link or reasonable likelihood is established and, for widespread breaches or serious incidents, no later than two days after awareness. The addressees, regulated actors, incident scope, and reporting procedure therefore differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared act of urgent incident notification is outweighed by materially different recipients, obligated parties, incident categories, and procedural triggers/deadlines; the norms do not impose substantially the same practical compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address ICT/data-security risk events and require organizational action by regulated entities, but their operative compliance duties are not the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a qualifying personal-data breach, generally within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, with reasons for delay. Norm B requires certain financial entities to establish and operate ICT-risk controls, including prompt identification and detection of ICT-risk sources and anomalies and rapid handling of ICT-related incidents; it does not require notification to a supervisory authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world action, recipient, and purpose differ: external breach notification to a regulator versus internal ICT-risk detection and incident-handling controls.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern supplying information as part of an incident or breach notification, but they require different substantive information to be supplied.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an early-warning notification to state whether the significant incident was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act, along with other specified early-warning details. Norm B requires a personal-data-breach notification to include the breach's nature, information sources, recommended mitigation measures, and— for the authority—its consequences and response measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required content and practical compliance action differ: A requires a causal-characterisation statement in an early warning to the CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B requires a fuller data-breach notification containing descriptive, contact, impact, and mitigation information for the supervisory authority and affected person.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to a data-related event by requiring organizational action concerning transaction or personal-data information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to promptly communicate a personal-data breach directly to affected data subjects (subject to the related exceptions and substitute public notice). Norm B requires data-reporting service providers to maintain systems that detect incomplete or erroneous transaction reports and request retransmission. The former is an urgent notification duty; the latter is an ongoing technical detection and correction capability.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: direct breach notification to individuals versus operating systems for validation, error detection, and retransmission requests.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires, on request, financial entities other than micro-enterprises to report changes implemented after a post-incident evaluation; Norm B requires high-risk AI providers (and in some cases deployers) to proactively notify market-surveillance authorities of serious incidents within specified deadlines.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required subject matter, trigger, and timing differ materially: post-evaluation remediation changes supplied on request versus mandatory incident notification within a fixed deadline.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to take action in response to ICT/AI-related incidents, but the concrete duties are different: Norm A requires ongoing registration of all ICT-related incidents and establishment of processes for monitoring, handling, follow-up, root-cause remediation, and prevention; Norm B requires submitting a report about a serious incident, subject to specified causal-link conditions and deadlines.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuous internal incident-management and recordkeeping obligation. Norm B is an external incident-reporting obligation triggered by a serious incident and, in the stated case, due immediately upon establishing or suspecting a causal link and no later than ten days after awareness (with the related paragraph providing the general fifteen-day rule).
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: internal registration/process management versus notification or reporting to the competent recipient.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by an incident and require the provider/controller to take a prompt compliance step, but the required steps are different.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires notifying the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach within (if possible) 72 hours, subject to a risk exception. Norm B requires the AI-system provider to investigate a serious incident, conduct a risk assessment, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and observe restrictions on altering the system; the related paragraph separately requires reporting the incident to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance action differs in substance: external incident notification under A versus investigation and remediation (with cooperation and procedural safeguards) under B. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by potentially harmful or abnormal digital events and concern the regulated entity’s response to such events.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires urgent notification of service recipients about significant incidents. Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for detecting abnormal activities, ICT incidents, network-performance issues, and physical single points of failure. One is an external communication duty; the other is an internal capability and testing duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: informing recipients versus establishing and testing detection mechanisms.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to perform or address a risk-impact assessment concerning risks associated with its regulated technology or ICT use.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an ongoing internal ICT-risk identification and assessment process, including annual scenario evaluation. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible entity to submit a report/notification concerning a serious or significant incident after becoming aware of it, subject to a specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity providing a trust service to report the significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority, with additional incident information and a substantially shorter 24-hour deadline. Norm B concerns serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system, requires reporting upon establishing or suspecting a causal link (specifically addressing death), and sets a deadline of immediately after that determination and no later than ten days after awareness; its recipient and reporting contents are not specified in the quoted provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action is not substantially the same in practice because the reporting duty has materially different scope and trigger conditions, recipients, and deadlines: a targeted 24-hour notification to two specified cybersecurity authorities versus an AI serious-incident report tied to a causal-link determination and due within ten days.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to notify affected individuals or clients promptly after a qualifying cyber/data incident, using an urgent notification duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires notification of the affected data subject about a personal-data breach where adverse privacy consequences are likely. Norm B requires financial entities to notify clients affected in their financial interests about a serious ICT incident and the measures taken to mitigate its negative effects; it also separately covers protective measures for clients potentially affected by a significant cyber threat. Thus B has a materially broader and more specific incident-and-mitigation communication obligation, while A is a privacy-breach notification duty subject to encryption and supervisory exceptions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required communication has materially different substantive content and scope: personal-data-breach notification to the data subject versus serious-ICT-incident notification to clients plus mitigation measures (and, separately, protective measures against cyber threats).

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information to a public authority in response to a security-related event or concern.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires broad, on-request or proactive provision of whatever data and information the Minister needs to prevent or end infringements of secure and reliable electronic access. Norm B requires trust-service providers to report significant incidents affecting their services to the CSIRT or competent authority, within 24 hours, as part of a structured incident-reporting process.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ substantively: general information disclosure to a Minister versus time-bound incident notification/reporting to an incident-response body, with specified incident content and follow-up reports.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to communicate or submit something to another designated body following a relevant regulatory event, but that is only a broad procedural similarity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a processor to promptly notify the controller of a personal-data breach. Norm B requires a conformity-assessment body to file an accreditation/notification request with the competent notifying authority in its Member State. verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: breach notification to a controller versus submission of a formal request for designation to a public authority.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een rapportageplicht met een vervangend voortgangsverslag zolang het incident voortduurt en een eindverslag binnen één maand na afhandeling. Norm B is een doorlopende beheer- en registratieplicht, inclusief organisatorische procedures en opvolging, zonder dezelfde verslagleggingsplicht of termijn.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational handling of cybersecurity-related information or events by regulated entities, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires reporting every significant incident to the competent recipient in accordance with the procedures and deadlines in Articles 26–29. Norm B requires maintaining capabilities and personnel to collect information about vulnerabilities, threats, and ICT incidents and analyze their likely effects on digital operational resilience; it is an internal capacity and analysis obligation, not an incident-reporting duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: external notification of significant incidents versus internal resourcing, information gathering, and impact analysis.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to or managing risks/incidents in the digital or personal-data sphere, but they do not require the same operational act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the content of a notification to the Dutch data-protection authority and affected person after a personal-data breach, including the breach's nature, information sources, mitigation measures, and— for the authority—effects and measures taken or proposed. Norm B requires financial entities to continuously identify ICT-risk sources and assess relevant cyber threats and vulnerabilities, plus periodically evaluate risk scenarios; it is an ongoing risk-identification and assessment duty, not an incident-notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: breach notification and prescribed notification contents versus continuous ICT-risk identification and assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the organisation to create and retain a written account concerning incidents or personal-data breaches, covering the event, its consequences, and remedial or mitigating measures, for regulatory oversight.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a formal final (or, while the incident continues, interim progress) report to be submitted to both the CSIRT and competent authority within a specified timeframe. Norm B requires documentation of all personal-data breaches so that the supervisory authority can inspect compliance; it does not, in the quoted provision, require submission of a report within a comparable deadline or to two designated recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in their operative compliance action: A is a time-bound external reporting/submission duty, whereas B is an ongoing documentation and record-keeping duty. The shared incident description does not make those actions substantially the same.

Norm B is an internal learning and remediation duty involving post-incident review and improvement; only specified non-micro financial entities must communicate resulting changes to authorities upon request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational handling of ICT/AI-related incidents, but their required actions are not the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires monitoring user activity and detecting ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents, especially cyberattacks. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to take organizational/operational measures addressing risks or incidents affecting their ICT or electronic communications services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires proportionate technical, operational, and organizational security measures to manage service-security risks and reduce the effects of security incidents. Norm B requires financial entities specifically to register all ICT incidents and significant cyber threats and to establish integrated procedures for monitoring, handling, follow-up, root-cause remediation, and prevention. The incident-recording and incident-management process in B is materially more specific than A's general preventive security-risk controls.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: general risk-based security controls versus mandatory incident registration and a structured incident-management and remediation process.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the covered provider/entity to implement appropriate and proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures to manage security risks and reduce the impact of security incidents on affected users, customers, or other services/networks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B expressly concerns providers of public electronic communications services and adds encryption where appropriate, a technology-state/risk-adjusted security level, and—through its related paragraph—specific availability measures for certain voice/internet-access services during outages or force majeure. Norm A applies to essential or important entities and expressly covers both risk control and incident prevention/impact limitation for service recipients and other services, without those additional sector-specific requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core compliance action is substantially the same: adopting proportionate technical, operational, and organisational measures to secure systems/services, control security risks, and limit incident consequences. The additional details in Norm B refine or extend that core duty rather than replace it with a materially different action.

verdict.evidence_span_b: nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen, waaronder in voorkomend geval versleuteling

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to or handling problematic data-related events, but they do not require the same operational compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the content of a breach notification to the supervisory authority and affected person, including the breach's nature, information sources, mitigation measures, and— for the authority—effects and remedial measures. Norm B requires data-reporting-service providers to maintain systems that check transaction reports, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission. One is a notification-content duty; the other is an ongoing technical detection and retransmission capability.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required actions differ in substance: breach notification disclosure versus automated/system-based transaction-report validation, error detection, and retransmission requests.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating or reporting serious ICT/AI-related incidents to external recipients after an incident occurs.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public. Norm B requires the incident itself to be reported to the designated national competent authority, and limits the reportable incidents for specified high-risk AI systems to the incidents defined in Article 3(49)(c). These are different recipients and different compliance actions: preparedness and stakeholder/public disclosure versus regulatory incident notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required action, recipient, and operational purpose differ substantially: crisis-communication planning and responsible disclosure under A versus direct notification to a designated national authority under B.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address protection of digital information and are directed at regulated entities, but their operative compliance duties are different: Norm A requires prompt incident reporting to specified authorities, while Norm B requires implementing ICT technologies and processes to prevent or mitigate data-security and availability risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered notification duty with a 24-hour deadline and named recipients (the CSIRT and competent authority). Norm B is an ongoing preventive technical and organizational control duty, with no reporting event, deadline, or specified recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world compliance action differs in substance: mandatory incident notification versus preventive implementation and operation of ICT security measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require measures aimed at preventing or limiting ICT/security-related harm, but they do not require the same concrete compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires specified public and private actors to provide the Minister, on request and proactively, with data and information needed for governmental measures concerning secure and reliable access to electronic services. Norm B requires certain financial entities to establish and operate an internal ICT-risk-management framework, including rapid identification and detection of ICT risks and anomalies and rapid handling of ICT incidents. One is an information-supply duty to a minister; the other is an ongoing internal operational risk-management duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required acts, recipients, and compliance mechanisms differ substantially: information disclosure to a public authority versus internal ICT monitoring, detection, and incident response.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to notify an affected external person or group promptly about a cyber/data-security incident or threat when the event may adversely affect them.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires informing potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and, if necessary, informing them of the threat itself. Norm B requires notifying the data subject of an actual personal-data breach when it is likely to have adverse privacy consequences; the duty may be unnecessary where effective protective measures make the data unintelligible.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required notification has a materially different substantive purpose and content: protective guidance concerning a significant cyber threat to service recipients versus breach notification to the affected data subject concerning likely privacy harm.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated party to notify a public authority about a qualifying incident, with the notification subject to a time limit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a controller to notify the competent data-protection supervisory authority of a personal-data breach, generally within 72 hours of becoming aware, subject to a risk-based exception and delay justification. Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to notify market-surveillance authorities of serious incidents, generally immediately and no later than 15 days after awareness (or within two days for specified widespread breaches/serious incidents), followed by investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation. The incident types, authorities, triggering conditions, deadlines, and ancillary duties differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared reporting form is outweighed by materially different substantive compliance obligations: different regulated actors and authorities, different qualifying events, different exceptions/triggers, different deadlines, and—under Norm B—mandatory post-notification investigation and corrective action.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern the handling or reporting of ICT/security incidents by regulated entities, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.

Norm B states that financial entities remain responsible for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents; the surrounding text also describes optional supervisory feedback, not a mandatory early-warning notification by the entity.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op handelen naar aanleiding van ICT-/gegevensincidenten door een organisatie die onder de norm valt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to submit a formal report concerning a cybersecurity/personal-data incident to a designated public authority after the incident or its discovery, subject to a specified reporting trigger and timing.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit an interim progress report instead of the final report when the incident is still ongoing, addressing the matters required for the final report, and then to submit the final report within one month after the incident is resolved. Norm B requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it (unless the breach is unlikely to pose a risk), with reasons for delay if late. The reports differ materially in purpose, content, recipient framework, and timing: ongoing-incident progress/final reporting versus prompt breach notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is substantively different: an incident-progress/final reporting regime tied to incident resolution versus a rapid personal-data-breach notification obligation tied to awareness.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by security incidents and concern security-related compliance by regulated entities, but their required actions are materially different: Norm A requires prompt incident notification to the CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident information; Norm B requires implementation of technical, operational, and organizational security-risk measures to limit incident consequences.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty with a 72-hour deadline (or 24 hours for the specified trust-service provider exception), whereas Norm B is an ongoing preventive risk-management duty and does not require reporting an incident to a public body.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: notification and information submission versus implementation of security controls and risk-management measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose a compliance duty triggered by a risk-related event or assessment, but their required actions are materially different: Norm A requires an entity to restrict procurement or use to products/services not supplied by a designated risky party, whereas Norm B requires reporting a serious AI incident to market-surveillance authorities within a specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supplier/product-use exclusion and substitution obligation concerning network and information systems; Norm B is an incident-notification obligation directed to public authorities, with immediate and maximum reporting deadlines.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to an incident by creating or maintaining incident-related compliance information, but they do not require the same operational act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to document every personal-data breach, including its facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so the supervisory authority can verify compliance. Norm B requires certain AI providers or deployers to actively notify Member State market-surveillance authorities of a serious incident, immediately and no later than two days after awareness. Documentation and external notification are substantively different duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: internal/compliance documentation of breaches versus time-bound reporting of serious incidents to a specified authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt notification after an incident or threat is identified, but the required notifications are directed to different recipients and serve different regulatory purposes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to send an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident-characterisation and contact information. Norm B requires a financial entity to inform potentially affected clients about a serious ICT-related incident, the mitigation measures taken, or—where applicable—protective measures for a significant cyberthreat.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different recipient and substantive content/purpose of the required communication: regulatory early warning to authorities versus customer-facing incident and mitigation/protection information.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: The substantive actions differ: Norm A is an internal incident-assessment and classification exercise based on specified impact criteria; Norm B is an external notification/reporting obligation, with immediate or scenario-specific deadlines of 15, 10, or 2 days.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different—internal classification and impact assessment versus external regulatory reporting—even though both are triggered by incidents and concern incident handling.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires urgent incident/security or misuse notification, including all necessary information; Norm B requires a conformity-assessment body to file an application for notification/designation with the competent notifying authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern a response to an event involving the addressee, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A grants an injured person a right to obtain compensation from the controller or processor for damage caused by a GDPR infringement. Norm B requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents to the competent authority, including initial, interim, and final reports under the referenced procedure and deadlines.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative actions, recipients, and legal functions differ substantially: compensation for suffered damage versus regulatory incident reporting.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting an incident to a designated external authority/body after awareness or identification of the incident, within a specified time limit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a substantive final incident report to both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, including a detailed description, severity and consequences, threat/root cause, mitigation measures, and possible cross-border effects. Norm B requires an incident notification by a high-risk AI provider or deployer to the relevant market-surveillance authorities; the cited provision primarily governs when that notification must be made, with special shorter deadlines for certain incidents, and does not impose the detailed final-report contents required by Norm A.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in substantive compliance action: A is a detailed final-reporting and, where necessary, progress-reporting duty to cybersecurity bodies, whereas B is a prompt serious-incident notification duty to market-surveillance authorities, with event-specific deadlines.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve organizational reporting-related compliance, but they do not require the same practical action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach within the specified timeframe (unless the risk exception applies), whereas Norm B requires the financial entity’s management body to establish internal enterprise-level reporting channels for gathering information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, planned material changes, and their effects.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern reporting an incident, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to submit a progress report instead of a final report when the incident is still ongoing, addressing the aspects required for the final report, and then submit the final report within one month after resolution. Norm B requires reporting a qualifying serious incident to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where it occurred; it does not impose the progress/final-report sequence or the one-month post-resolution deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required recipient, reporting procedure, timing, and report type differ materially: A is a staged progress/final reporting duty for an ongoing incident, while B is a serious-incident notification to a designated national authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern a legally triggered follow-up action that must be carried out after the relevant event or condition occurs, with a time-related limitation or deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the daily imposition of a coercive penalty on a critical ICT third-party service provider until its obligations are fulfilled, for no more than six months after notification of the penalty decision. Norm B requires providers (and in some cases deployers) to report serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities, promptly and within specified maximum periods (normally 15 days, or shorter periods for certain incidents). The former is enforcement through an ongoing monetary coercion; the latter is an incident-reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: continuing imposition of a coercive fine versus submitting a regulatory incident notification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require organizational/technical risk-management activity concerning security or ICT risks, including measures or processes intended to control or reduce those risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires providers of public electronic communications networks or services to implement prescribed technical, operational, and organizational measures to manage security risks and limit the consequences of security incidents affecting national security or public order. Norm B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be periodically and incident-triggeredly documented and evaluated, continuously improved, and its evaluation report submitted on request; it is a governance, review, and reporting duty rather than the substantive implementation of security-risk controls itself.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: A is implementation of prescribed security-risk controls, while B is recurring documentation, evaluation, improvement, and possible reporting of an ICT-risk-management framework.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require structured testing or evaluation activities intended to identify risks or vulnerabilities and support their mitigation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires other financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme as part of ICT-risk management. Norm B requires providers of systemically risky general-purpose AI models to perform and document model evaluations and to assess and mitigate Union-level systemic risks, while also imposing incident-information reporting and cybersecurity duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in their substantive object and compliance output: A is an ongoing organisational testing-programme requirement, whereas B is a model-specific evaluation, systemic-risk mitigation, incident-reporting, and cybersecurity package.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take action in response to ICT/cyber risk or incidents, but their actual compliance duties are not the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires prompt incident reporting to the CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident information and, where applicable, an initial assessment and indicators of compromise. Norm B requires an ongoing internal risk-management process: permanent identification of ICT-risk sources, assessment of threats and vulnerabilities, and at least annual evaluation of risk scenarios. It does not require reporting an incident to an authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required operational action and recipient of the action differ substantially: external incident notification within a short deadline versus continuous internal ICT-risk identification and periodic risk assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern responding to a cybersecurity or personal-data incident by taking a legally relevant step after an adverse event, but they do not require the same practical action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires notifying the Dutch data-protection authority and affected individual(s), with specified information and proposed or taken remedial measures. Norm B requires financial entities to classify cyber threats as significant using specified impact, client/counterparty, and geographic criteria; it does not itself require notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: external incident notification and content disclosure versus internal classification of cyber threats.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about a personal-data breach to affected individuals, with the communication triggered by the breach.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-assessment handling by the regulated entity, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address organizational responses to ICT/data-security events, but they require different operational measures: Norm A requires documenting personal-data breaches and their facts, effects, and corrective measures; Norm B requires deploying sufficient resources and capabilities for ongoing monitoring and detection of user activity, ICT anomalies, and ICT-related incidents.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address organizational handling and reporting of significant/ICT-related incidents, including detecting or identifying incidents and ensuring that they are reported.

verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world compliance action differs in substance: external reporting of requested or voluntarily supplied information versus internal, continuous risk identification and assessment.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an early warning to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority containing specific incident-characterisation information, including whether the incident was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act. Norm B requires the provider to notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority immediately of a security breach adversely affecting the protection of personal data processed in connection with the service.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in recipient and substantive content: Norm A is an early-warning communication with specified incident details, while Norm B is an immediate personal-data security-breach notification to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in the context of digital/cybersecurity risks and concern information relevant to protecting digital services, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires specified public and private actors to provide the Minister, on request and proactively, with the data and information needed for governmental measures against breaches of secure and reliable access to electronic services. Norm B requires financial entities to classify cyber threats as significant using specified criteria concerning critical services, affected clients or counterparties, and geographic spread. One is an information-disclosure duty to a minister; the other is an internal threat-classification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: supplying information to a government authority versus classifying cyber threats according to prescribed criteria.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to a harmful or serious incident by communicating information to a public authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a substantive breach notification containing specified information to the data-protection authority and affected person, including the breach's nature, information sources, recommended mitigation, and—toward the authority—effects and measures taken or proposed. Norm B requires reporting each serious incident during real-world AI testing to the market-surveillance authority, while separately requiring immediate risk mitigation, suspension, or termination of testing and a recall procedure. The reporting duties and their required content and regulatory contexts differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actual compliance actions are not substantially the same: A is a detailed personal-data-breach notification duty to two recipients, whereas B is an incident-reporting duty to one market-surveillance authority embedded in a broader immediate risk-control and testing-termination regime.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take follow-up action after a serious ICT/AI incident, but the required actions are not the same: Norm A requires post-incident evaluation and, on request, reporting implemented improvements to competent authorities; Norm B requires the provider to promptly investigate the incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities and preserving the system for later causal evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ex post review-and-disclosure obligation focused on analyzing disruption causes, assessing procedures and measures, identifying improvements, and communicating implemented changes upon request. Norm B is an immediate incident-investigation obligation focused on investigating the incident and system, assessing risk, taking corrective measures, cooperating with authorities, and avoiding potentially prejudicial system modifications without prior notice.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core compliance action differs in substance: Norm A requires a post-incident evaluation and possible disclosure of resulting changes, whereas Norm B requires an urgent investigation with risk assessment and corrective action, plus procedural safeguards during that investigation.
