verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in actor role, recipient, incident context, and substantive purpose/content: A is customer/service-recipient notification by an essential or important entity; B is regulatory reporting and operational risk-control by an AI provider or potential provider during real-world testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core compliance action on the same actor for the same event family. A concerns notifying service recipients about significant service-affecting incidents; B concerns reporting serious testing incidents to a market-surveillance authority and taking specified containment or testing-termination measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve providing information to a competent authority concerning serious/significant ICT-related incidents, but A requires incident reporting and B requires an on-request estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a mandatory, time-bound incident-reporting sequence (including a 24-hour report for the specified trust-service-provider case) containing incident facts, assessment, impact, indicators, causes, and mitigation measures. Norm B is an on-request provision of a financial estimate covering aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same actor role: A applies to a trust-service provider reporting significant incidents affecting its trust services, while B applies to financial entities other than micro-enterprises. They also require materially different outputs and purposes: incident reporting versus an aggregated annual cost-and-loss estimate.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern cybersecurity and protection against ICT/data-related incidents, but A requires reporting each significant incident, whereas B requires implementing ICT technologies and processes to prevent or mitigate specified security and data risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty for essential or important entities under the NIS2 framework; Norm B is a preventive ICT-security control duty for financial entities under DORA. The triggering event is not the same: A presupposes that a significant incident has occurred, while B requires preventive measures irrespective of a particular incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: A requires an essential or important entity to report significant incidents, while B requires a financial entity to implement/use ICT technologies and processes that prevent or limit security and data risks. Similar cybersecurity subject matter does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Om de in lid 2 bedoelde doelstellingen te verwezenlijken, maken financiële entiteiten gebruik van ICT-technologieën en -processen die geschikt zijn overeenkomstig artikel 4.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A legt aansprakelijkheid voor schade door onrechtmatige verwerking op; norm B verplicht tot permanente identificatie en beoordeling van ICT-risico’s en jaarlijkse evaluatie van risicoscenario’s.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft civielrechtelijke aansprakelijkheid na schade door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op de AVG; norm B betreft een doorlopende ICT-risico-identificatie- en beoordelingsplicht voor financiële entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde verb-level actie, noch hetzelfde type trigger of dezelfde actorrol: aansprakelijkheid voor schade door onrechtmatige verwerking versus preventief ICT-risicobeheer door financiële entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico, met name de wederzijdse risicoblootstelling ten aanzien van andere financiële entiteiten, en beoordelen de cyberdreigingen en ICT-kwetsbaarheden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating a serious incident, but A requires financial entities to inform potentially affected clients about a serious ICT-related incident and mitigation measures, whereas B requires high-risk AI-system providers to report serious incidents to Member State market-surveillance authorities, with specified timing and follow-up procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in actor, recipient, regulatory purpose, and required content: client-facing incident/mitigation information under A versus authority-facing regulatory incident reporting under B.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core reporting duty; the shared serious-incident trigger and communication element do not make the obligations the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern measures addressing the consequences or communication of security/ICT incidents, but A requires preventive risk-control measures while B requires maintaining crisis-communication plans enabling disclosure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a technical, operational and organisational risk-mitigation duty imposed on public electronic communications providers; Norm B is a crisis-communication planning and disclosure-enablement duty imposed on financial entities, directed to clients, counterparties and potentially the public.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different underlying action; the shared ICT/security-incident context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling/reporting-related controls around data or transaction incidents, but A requires notifying a supervisory authority of a personal-data breach, whereas B requires data-reporting service providers to maintain systems that check transaction reports and request retransmission where needed.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered breach notification duty to a supervisory authority, with a 72-hour deadline; Norm B is an ongoing systems-and-controls obligation concerning completeness, omissions, apparent errors, and retransmission of transaction reports, with no specified deadline or authority recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, and actor role; A concerns breach notification by a controller, while B concerns detection and retransmission-request systems maintained by data-reporting service providers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern measures connected with protecting network and information systems, but Norm A imposes a ministerial restriction on using specified suppliers' products or services, whereas Norm B requires certain financial entities, on request, to communicate changes made after post-incident evaluations to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive supplier-use restriction imposed by a minister; Norm B is a post-incident review-and-information-sharing duty directed to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering circumstances, actor roles, and compliance content differ materially; the apparent similarity is limited to a broad cybersecurity context.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires providers of public electronic communications services to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures, potentially including encryption, to manage security risks and minimise the effects of security incidents. Norm B states that financial entities remain responsible for handling and the consequences of ICT-related incidents reported under Article 19(1), while addressing supervisory feedback and corrective measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different core duties: proactive implementation of security measures versus continued responsibility and supervisory follow-up after reporting an ICT incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action taken in response to an ICT/AI-related incident, but A requires internal data-integrity controls during recovery, whereas B requires reporting a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities, followed by investigation and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal recovery and data-integrity control duty; Norm B is an external regulatory notification duty for serious AI incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires financial entities to perform recovery-time data-integrity checks, while B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities. verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating about an incident, but A requires the provider to notify affected individuals of a personal-data breach, whereas B requires a financial entity to implement an ICT-incident communications strategy and designate a spokesperson for public and media communications.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate, conditional notification duty directed to affected data subjects; Norm B is an organisational communications-strategy and spokesperson duty directed generally to the public and media, with no specified incident-notification deadline or identical content requirement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient and substantive purpose/content; the shared incident-related context is insufficient to make them duplicate or merely related reporting burdens.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling information connected with digital-security risks, but Norm A requires supplying information to the Minister, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish internal incident-management processes.

Norm B is an internal ICT-incident governance and record-keeping duty, covering registration, monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and root-cause remediation; it does not require reporting to an authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor scope and core action: Norm A imposes provision of information to a minister, while Norm B imposes internal registration and incident-management processes on financial entities. The shared security-related subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to a competent public authority in connection with an ICT/AI-related incident or disruption. Norm A requires non-micro financial entities, on request, to communicate changes implemented after post-incident evaluations; Norm B requires reporting a qualifying serious incident itself to a designated national authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a post-incident, request-based disclosure about remedial changes following an evaluation of a disruption to core activities. Norm B is an incident-reporting duty concerning specified serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems, directed to the authority in the Member State where the incident occurred.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in their underlying action, actor scope, and required content/purpose: post-incident remedial-change disclosure on request versus reporting the serious incident itself. The shared incident-related context and authority-facing channel do not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible entity to make a report/notification concerning a serious or significant incident. However, Norm A requires a detailed incident report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, including specified technical, impact, and cross-border-effect information; Norm B sets a deadline for reporting a serious incident involving death where a causal link or suspected causal link to a high-risk AI system exists, but does not specify the recipient or reporting contents in the quoted provision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns significant incidents affecting essential or important entities and requires reporting to both a CSIRT and competent authority with detailed incident information. Norm B concerns serious incidents involving death linked, or suspected to be linked, to a high-risk AI system and sets a ten-day maximum deadline for the provider or deployer; its recipient and substantive reporting requirements are not stated here.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-reporting pattern and comparable regulated-entity role, but the triggering incident conditions, reporting purpose, deadline, recipient, and required content differ substantially; the text does not establish that the same report must be prepared or submitted twice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: In both norms, the designated provider or its authorized representative must provide requested information and remains responsible for information that is incomplete, incorrect, or misleading.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different regulatory/event context; the shared verb-level action and similar responsibility rule do not make the duties the same compliance obligation.

These are not the same compliance action.

Norm B is an ongoing internal ICT-risk-management and incident-detection/response measure, with no reporting recipient or comparable deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor scope/role, recipient, and purpose: A requires external incident notification, whereas B requires ongoing internal risk-management, detection, and response capabilities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an entity to implement broad, risk-based cybersecurity measures protecting network and information systems and their physical environment against incidents. Norm B requires a public electronic communications provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a security breach affecting the protection of processed personal data.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb level and in compliance purpose: implementing comprehensive protective measures versus notifying a data-protection authority of a qualifying security breach. verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a record-keeping/documentation duty concerning personal-data breaches; Norm B is a preventive and operational ICT-incident management framework duty, not a duty to create the same breach records.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to ICT/AI-related incidents, but Norm A requires ongoing monitoring and detection capabilities, whereas Norm B requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident, conduct a risk assessment, take corrective measures, and cooperate with authorities after reporting it.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating or reporting information about a serious incident or breach without delay, but they impose different substantive duties: Norm A requires the controller to notify the affected data subject of a personal-data breach; Norm B requires providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models to keep and document relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures, and report it to the AI Office and, where appropriate, national competent authorities.

Norm B is an ongoing record-keeping/documentation duty plus regulatory reporting concerning serious incidents and possible corrective measures, addressed to authorities. The actors, recipients, and reportable content therefore differ materially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same compliance work: the actor role differs (controller versus provider of a systemic-risk general-purpose AI model), the recipient differs (data subject versus AI Office/national authorities), and the required content and purpose differ (breach notification to protect the individual versus documented regulatory reporting on serious incidents and corrective measures). The shared urgent incident-reporting theme is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, with specified incident-related information and a 24-hour fallback deadline. B requires central securities depositories and central counterparties to perform vulnerability assessments before deploying or redeploying specified applications, infrastructure components, or ICT services.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/cybersecurity risk, but Norm A requires preventive technical and process measures to protect availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, and data. Norm B requires specified banks and financial-market entities to submit ICT-incident notifications, including voluntary notifications, additionally to the designated sectoral CSIRT. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information to a public authority in response to a potentially harmful incident or security-related situation, but A is a broad information-supply duty on request or on the entity’s own initiative, while B is a specific notification of a personal-data breach.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about an incident, but A requires notifying service recipients of significant incidents, whereas B specifies the required contents of a personal-data-breach notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and the affected person, including consequences and remedial measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security governance in response to an ICT-related incident, but A requires an early-warning notification/report to the CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B requires documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework and submitting an evaluation report on request.

Norm B is a periodic and serious-incident-triggered internal governance/documentation and evaluation duty, with a possible report submission on request; it is not the same notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and responsible actor differ: A requires an essential or important entity to send an early warning about a significant incident, while B requires a financial entity within the simplified framework to document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework. The shared ICT-incident context and possible competent-authority involvement do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an entity to promptly inform its service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and where necessary to inform them of the threat itself. B requires certain financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme, implemented on a risk-based basis. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent outward communication duty to potentially affected service recipients concerning a significant cyber threat; Norm B is an ongoing internal governance and testing-programme duty concerning digital operational resilience.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the operative action and the triggering subject matter: A concerns communicating threat-response measures to service recipients, while B concerns establishing, maintaining, and evaluating an internal resilience-testing programme. The shared broad digital/cyber context is insufficient to create a duplicate or related reporting burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor de beoordeling van de paraatheid ten aanzien van de behandeling van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, de omschrijving van zwakheden, gebreken en lacunes in de digitale operationele weerbaarheid, en de snelle uitvoering van corrigerende maatregelen zorgen andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen, rekening houdend met de criteria in artikel 4, lid 2, voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid als integrerend onderdeel van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer als bedoeld in artikel 6.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit a final (or, where the incident continues, progress) incident report to its CSIRT and competent authority, containing specified incident details and mitigation information. Norm B requires data-reporting-service providers to maintain systems that check transaction reports for completeness, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission. These are not the same underlying compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty triggered by a cybersecurity incident and directed to authorities/CSIRT; Norm B is an ongoing systems-and-controls duty concerning the validation and retransmission of transaction reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both the actor duty and the event/purpose: A requires post-incident reporting, while B requires operational systems for checking transaction reports and requesting retransmission.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible entity to urgently notify/report a security-related incident to a public recipient, with accompanying information. Norm A specifically requires a significant incident affecting the provision of a trust service to be reported to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B requires notification to the Minister of a breach of security or integrity of the entity’s own electronic service, or misuse/improper use of access, together with all necessary information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a significant incident affecting a trust service and requires reporting to both a CSIRT and competent authority, with a 24-hour fallback deadline and the fuller Article 27(1) information package. Norm B concerns breaches or misuse involving an entity’s own electronic service and requires notification to the Minister with all necessary information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles are not the same: Norm A applies to an essential or important entity offering a trust service, while Norm B applies to a public administrative body or designated organisation. The event descriptions and reporting content also differ materially. Although both involve urgent notification of security-related incidents to an authority, the text does not establish that the same actor must perform the same report for the same event under both norms.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires financial entities to perform data-integrity checks and reconciliations during recovery from an ICT-related incident. verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A requires internal data-integrity checks during ICT-incident recovery, while B requires reporting a serious testing incident to a market-surveillance authority and taking specified risk measures. They also concern different actors and different triggering-event contexts.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a post-incident report, whereas B requires financial entities to use ICT technologies and processes that prevent or mitigate data and availability/security risks. The shared cybersecurity subject matter does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: de verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke over een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens. B: financiële entiteiten classificeren cyberdreigingen als significant aan de hand van impact-, doelgroep- en geografische criteria.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een meldingsplicht aan een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke na kennisname van een persoonsgegevensinbreuk; norm B is een interne classificatiebeoordeling van cyberdreigingen door financiële entiteiten. De teksten leggen geen identieke rapportage- of meldingshandeling op.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde kernactie en niet dezelfde actorrol; bovendien is A een melding aan een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, terwijl B een interne classificatie van cyberdreigingen betreft.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten classificeren cyberdreigingen als significant op basis van de mate waarin de risicovolle diensten, waaronder de transacties en verrichtingen van de financiële entiteit, als cruciaal kunnen worden aangemerkt, het aantal en/of de relevantie van de beoogde cliënten of financiële tegenpartijen en de geografische spreiding van de risicogebieden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an entity’s handling of information about cyber-related risks or incidents, but Norm A requires an urgent early-warning notification to specified authorities, while Norm B requires maintaining capabilities and personnel to collect and analyse information for digital operational resilience.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered external reporting duty with a 24-hour deadline and specified recipients; Norm B is an ongoing internal capability and resource requirement, with no reporting recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad cyber-risk/incident subject matter and actor category, but different core actions and compliance purposes: urgent authority notification versus maintaining capabilities and personnel for information collection and analysis.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen, en om de waarschijnlijke gevolgen ervan voor hun digitale operationele weerbaarheid te analyseren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information to a public authority in connection with an adverse ICT/security-related event or its consequences, but they require different substantive work: A requires providing information needed by the Minister to prevent or end infringements of secure and reliable access to electronic services; B requires, on request, communicating changes implemented after post-incident evaluations of serious ICT incidents disrupting core activities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad, potentially proactive information-supply duty concerning measures to prevent or terminate infringements of secure electronic access. Norm B is a sector-specific, request-based duty to report implemented improvements following a post-incident evaluation of a serious ICT incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same actor role: A applies to public bodies, designated organisations, recognised holders, issuers and service providers, whereas B applies to financial entities. Their information content and compliance purpose also differ substantially, so this is not the same work repeated merely for an additional recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen
verdict.evidence_span_b: delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het opnemen van operationele conclusies uit tests en incidentanalyse in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces; norm B vereist het melden van een ernstig incident aan een aangewezen nationale bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een interne ICT-risicobeheer- en evaluatieverplichting zonder ontvanger of deadline; norm B is een externe incidentmeldingsplicht aan een nationale autoriteit voor specifieke ernstige incidenten bij bepaalde hoog-risico-AI-systemen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en de betrokken actorrol verschillen: A betreft interne verwerking van lessen uit tests/incidentanalyse door bepaalde financiële entiteiten, terwijl B externe melding van een ernstig incident door de aanbieder of exploitant van een specifiek hoog-risico-AI-systeem vereist. De gedeelde incidentcontext is onvoldoende voor dubbele compliance-last.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to an adverse incident by recording or reporting information and taking compliance-related action, but they do not require the same underlying work: Norm A requires the controller to document personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, while Norm B requires reporting serious incidents found during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority and also requires immediate risk mitigation, suspension/termination, and a recall procedure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a documentation duty concerning all personal-data breaches, including facts, consequences, and corrective measures; Norm B is an incident-reporting and operational risk-response duty concerning serious incidents during real-world testing of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the triggering event and the operative obligation: Norm A covers personal-data breaches and requires documentation by a data controller; Norm B covers serious incidents during real-world testing and requires reporting by an AI provider or potential provider, plus immediate mitigation or testing suspension/termination and a recall procedure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to maintain records of incident-related events: A requires a register/overview of all personal-data breaches, while B requires registration of all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and related incident-management processes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is specifically a personal-data-breach overview that must contain specified facts and data; Norm B is a broader ICT-incident and significant-cyber-threat registration and management process, including monitoring, treatment, follow-up, root-cause documentation and remediation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern a similar incident-recording activity and overlapping security-event domain, but they apply to different regulated actor categories and require materially different records and purposes. They therefore warrant review as related burdens, not a finding that the same compliance work must be repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an actor to communicate information about an incident, but A requires informing service recipients about significant incidents affecting service provision, while B requires reporting a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority, subject to a risk exception and possible delay justification.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in purpose, recipient, and required content: A is customer/service-recipient information about service impact; B is regulatory breach notification concerning risks to individuals' rights and freedoms, with a 72-hour deadline and delay justification.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-reporting family and actor role, but different recipients, purposes, content, and deadlines; therefore related rather than duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a notification/report concerning an adverse incident: A requires notifying the affected person of a personal-data breach, while B requires reporting a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, with a special deadline where a person has died.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ materially in recipient, incident type, and required reporting purpose/content: A is an individual data-subject notification about a personal-data breach; B is an incident report under the AI Act concerning a serious incident, specifically death and a causal or suspected causal link to a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-reporting family and comparable regulated-provider role, but not the same compliance work: the data-subject breach notification in A and the serious-AI-incident report in B have different recipients, purposes, and substantive content. The different recipient alone is not decisive; the low content overlap is.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational follow-up after an ICT/security-related incident, but they require different actions: A requires documenting personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, while B requires conducting post-incident evaluations, analyzing causes, identifying improvements, and, on request, communicating implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR personal-data-breach documentation duty directed at enabling supervisory verification; Norm B is a DORA operational-resilience post-incident evaluation and improvement duty following serious ICT-related disruption, with possible disclosure of resulting changes on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general security/ICT incident family and broadly the same regulated-entity role, but the core actions and required content differ: comprehensive breach documentation under A versus post-incident causal analysis, effectiveness assessment, improvement identification, and potentially communicating implemented changes under B. The duties therefore create related review/compliance work, not the same work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid als bedoeld in artikel 11.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern managing ICT/security risk, but Norm A requires urgent notification of a qualifying personal-data security breach, whereas Norm B requires ongoing identification and assessment of ICT risks, threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty triggered by a security breach affecting personal-data protection and addressed to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens. Norm B is a continuous, periodic internal risk-identification and assessment duty with no reporting recipient and no breach trigger.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, and compliance purpose: urgent breach notification to a data-protection authority versus continuous and annual ICT-risk assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require a compliance action by a regulated entity in response to a digital-risk context: A requires communicating a personal-data breach to the affected data subject; B requires conducting vulnerability assessments before deploying or redeploying specified ICT applications, infrastructure components, or supporting ICT services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent external breach notification to the data subject after a high-risk personal-data breach. Norm B is a preventive technical assessment performed before ICT deployment or redeployment; it is not a notification or reporting duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering events, and actor roles differ: A concerns a controller notifying a data subject of a high-risk personal-data breach, whereas B concerns central securities depositories and central counterparties conducting vulnerability assessments before ICT deployment or redeployment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen verrichten kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen voordat nieuwe of bestaande toepassingen en infrastructuurcomponenten, en ICT-diensten ter ondersteuning van kritieke of belangrijke functies van de financiële entiteit worden ingezet of opnieuw worden ingezet.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A grants an injured person a right to receive compensation from a controller or processor; Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for promptly detecting anomalous activities, ICT incidents, network-performance issues, and physical single points of failure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a private compensation/liability right arising after damage caused by a GDPR infringement, whereas Norm B is a preventive ICT-risk detection and testing obligation imposed on financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different kinds of duties on different actors in response to different legal situations: compensation for GDPR-related damage versus preventive detection and testing of ICT risks and incidents.
verdict.evidence_span_a: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt communication concerning a potentially harmful cyber/data-related event, but A requires informing affected service recipients about protective measures (and, if needed, the threat), whereas B requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach, with a possible late-notification explanation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in actor, recipient, purpose, and substantive content: A is protective information to potentially affected service recipients about measures against a significant cyber threat; B is regulatory breach notification by a controller to the data-protection supervisory authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core action differ, and the required content and recipient are materially different; the shared broad incident context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling and recording information about personal-data breaches, including the breach, its consequences, and measures taken or recommended to address or mitigate it. However, Norm A requires a notification to the supervisory authority and affected person, while Norm B requires the controller to document all breaches so the supervisory authority can verify compliance.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an outward notification duty to specified recipients and includes information about the breach, information sources, and recommended mitigation measures; Norm B is an internal documentation duty for all breaches, maintained to enable supervisory compliance checks.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same personal-data-breach event family, but different core actions and actor roles: notification by the provider versus documentation by the controller; the overlap in breach facts, consequences, and measures creates related compliance work rather than identical reporting work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het rapporteren van incidentgerelateerde informatie, maar norm A vereist een periodiek, geanonimiseerd en geaggregeerd samenvattend verslag over eerder gemelde gebeurtenissen, terwijl norm B vereist dat aanbieders relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een centraal contactpunt dat aan Enisa periodieke geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde samenvattingen van meldingen verstrekt; norm B betreft aanbieders van AI-modellen met systeemrisico die incidentinformatie en corrigerende maatregelen rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en eventueel nationale autoriteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De actorrol en de concrete rapportageverplichting verschillen wezenlijk: een centraal contactpunt maakt periodieke geaggregeerde rapporten voor Enisa, terwijl een AI-modelaanbieder incidentinformatie en corrigerende maatregelen onverwijld rapporteert aan AI-toezichthouders.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern consequences of a legally relevant event, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Norm A requires an entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, while Norm B gives an injured person a right to receive compensation from a controller or processor.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-bound incident-reporting duty imposed on an essential or important entity providing a trust service; Norm B is a private-law right to compensation for material or non-material damage caused by a GDPR infringement.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the norms do not require the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to take organizational/operational steps concerning security or ICT-related incidents: A requires security-risk mitigation measures, while B requires registration and incident-management processes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive security-risk mitigation duty for providers of public electronic communications networks or services, focused on limiting effects on national security or public order. Norm B is an ICT-incident management and record-keeping duty for financial entities, focused on registering incidents and significant cyber threats and addressing root causes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A requires implementing technical, operational, and organizational security measures, whereas B requires registering ICT incidents and establishing processes for monitoring, handling, follow-up, and remediation. The shared incident/security context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling personal-data breaches, but Norm A requires maintaining an internal register containing breach facts and specified data, whereas Norm B requires notifying the competent supervisory authority of a breach, generally within 72 hours, with reasons for delay if late.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing internal record-keeping duty; Norm B is a conditional external notification duty to the supervisory authority with a 72-hour deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family overlaps (personal-data breach), but the core actions, actor roles, recipients, and required content differ: maintaining an overview versus notifying a supervisory authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require incident-related reporting/notification by the regulated entity to a public authority, but A specifies the information that must be included in a personal-data-breach notification, while B requires staged reporting of a significant service incident, including an early warning, incident report, updates, and final report.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns notification of a personal-data breach to the Dutch data-protection authority and affected person, with prescribed breach-information and mitigation content. Norm B concerns significant incidents affecting service provision, reported to a CSIRT or competent authority through a time-sequenced reporting process; for trust-service providers, the report is due within 24 hours.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-reporting family and broadly comparable authority-facing reporting duty, but the triggering incidents, recipients, deadlines, and required report content are not sufficiently identical for DUPLICATE_BURDEN.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to communicate information about a security-related incident or misuse event. However, Norm A requires a progress report instead of a final incident report when the incident is ongoing, followed by a final report after resolution; Norm B requires immediate notification of a security/integrity breach or misuse of access and provision of all necessary information to the Minister.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a structured follow-up reporting duty to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, with specified incident details, causes, mitigation measures, and possible cross-border effects, and a one-month post-resolution final-report deadline. Norm B is an immediate notification duty to the Minister concerning a breach or misuse of the entity’s own electronic service, with all necessary information.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad security-incident event family, but the actor categories, reporting purposes, recipients, timing, and required content are not sufficiently identical to constitute the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action taken in the context of an ICT/cyber incident, but Norm A requires urgent communication to potentially affected service recipients about protective measures and, if necessary, the threat; Norm B requires financial entities to perform controls and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery or data reconstruction to preserve data integrity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external information/notification duty to service recipients; Norm B is an internal recovery and data-integrity control duty. They differ in action, purpose, and recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action: informing potentially affected service recipients versus performing recovery/data-integrity controls. The actor roles also differ: an essential or important entity under Norm A versus a financial entity under Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address organizational handling of potentially harmful digital events, but A requires prompt notification of a personal-data breach to the controller, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain and test mechanisms for detecting anomalous activities, ICT incidents, performance issues, and physical single points of failure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty imposed on a processor; Norm B is a preventive detection-capability and testing duty imposed on a financial entity.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and actor roles differ: prompt breach notification to the controller versus maintaining and regularly testing detection mechanisms. Similarity of the digital-incident context does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren, met inbegrip van kwesties op het gebied van ICT-netwerkprestaties en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, en om potentiële zwakke fysieke punten (“single points of failure”) te identificeren.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern serious/ICT-related incidents and, in a broad sense, incident-related handling or information. However, Norm A assigns continuing responsibility for handling consequences, while Norm B requires providers to keep, document, and promptly report information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a responsibility/oversight provision for financial entities after reports under Article 19(1); Norm B is an affirmative recordkeeping, documentation, and reporting duty for providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met ICT-incidenten en leggen een verplichting op aan financiële-sectoractoren, maar A vereist documenteren/evalueren van het ICT-risicobeheerkader en op verzoek verslaglegging aan de bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B een incidentmelding aan een aangewezen CSIRT vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft evaluatie en verslaglegging over het ICT-risicobeheerkader; norm B betreft melding van ICT-incidenten aan een sector-CSIRT.
verdict.criterion_fired: Zelfde algemene ICT-incidentcontext en vergelijkbare financiële-sectoractoren, maar verschillende kernhandelingen, ontvangers en inhoud: kader-evaluatie/verslag tegenover incidentmelding.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd
verdict.evidence_span_b: doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information about cyber/data incidents, but A requires the service provider to notify the affected individual directly, whereas B requires the central contact point to submit a periodic, anonymised and aggregated report to ENISA.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate, individual privacy notification by the provider to the data subject; Norm B is a quarterly systemic report by the central contact point to ENISA aggregating previously reported incidents, threats and near-incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not imposed on the same actor role: A is imposed on the provider and concerns direct notification of an affected data subject, while B is imposed on the central contact point and concerns an aggregated report to ENISA. The different reporting purpose and content also mean the work is not the same compliance work repeated.
