verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report instead of the final report while the incident continues, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. B requires a financial entity to maintain capabilities and personnel to collect information about vulnerabilities, cyber threats and ICT-related incidents and analyse their likely effects on digital operational resilience.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-triggered reporting duty to a CSIRT and competent authority, with specified report content and timing; B is an ongoing organisational capability and analysis requirement, with no reporting recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the actor role and the core action: A requires incident reporting, whereas B requires maintaining resources and capabilities for information gathering and analysis. The shared incident/cyber-threat subject matter is insufficient to create duplicate or related reporting burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid. Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen, en om de waarschijnlijke gevolgen ervan voor hun digitale operationele weerbaarheid te analyseren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security incidents, but Norm A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under the procedures in Articles 26–29, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to deploy sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity and the occurrence of ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents, especially cyberattacks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty; Norm B is an ongoing detection/monitoring and capability-allocation duty. The reporting content, recipient, and deadline for Norm A are supplied by Articles 26–29, while Norm B does not require a report in the quoted provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and actor roles differ: reporting significant incidents versus maintaining monitoring capabilities for ICT anomalies and incidents. Similar incident subject matter does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require reporting an incident to a public authority, but they concern different reporting regimes: GDPR personal-data-breach notification by a controller versus AI serious-incident notification by a provider or, where applicable, a deployer/user responsible for use.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The triggering incidents, obligated actors, recipients, and reporting content differ. Norm B concerns serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems and reporting to market-surveillance authorities; Norm A concerns personal-data breaches and reporting to the competent data-protection supervisory authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the shared reporting form and broadly similar incident-triggered timing do not make the underlying compliance duty the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het verstrekken van informatie aan een overheidsinstantie, maar norm A legt geen meldingsplicht op: zij bevestigt slechts dat financiële entiteiten verantwoordelijk blijven voor reeds gemelde ICT-incidenten. Norm B verplicht de gebruiksverantwoordelijke daarentegen de resultaten van een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling en een ingevuld sjabloon aan de markttoezichtautoriteit te melden.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft verantwoordelijkheid voor de behandeling en gevolgen van reeds gemelde ICT-gerelateerde incidenten; norm B betreft een voorafgaande grondrechteneffectbeoordeling van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem en kennisgeving van de resultaten daarvan.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, gebeurtenisfamilie of actorrol. Norm A bevat bovendien geen zelfstandige rapportage- of kennisgevingsplicht, terwijl norm B een concrete kennisgeving aan de markttoezichtautoriteit vereist.
verdict.evidence_span_a: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a public electronic communications service provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying security breach. B primarily governs supervisory feedback after a financial entity's ICT-incident notification and confirms that the financial entity remains responsible for handling the incident and its consequences; it does not impose the same notification duty as A.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an immediate breach-notification duty on a communications-service provider to a data-protection authority. Norm B concerns supervisory feedback and continuing responsibility for ICT incidents reported under Article 19(1), involving financial entities and a competent authority; it does not itself require the entity to make the notification described in A.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and operative duty differ: A requires the provider to notify an authority, whereas B describes the authority's feedback and the financial entity's continuing responsibility after an ICT-incident report; the shared incident context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible entity to report a serious/significant incident to a public authority or incident-reporting body.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns significant incidents affecting the provision of services and requires a staged, detailed cybersecurity incident-reporting package; Norm B concerns serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system, specifically death, and requires reporting after a causal link (or suspected link) is established.
verdict.criterion_fired: The reporting verbs and broad incident context overlap, but the actor scope and substantive triggering incidents differ: A is a trust-service provider reporting significant incidents affecting trust services, while B is a provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system reporting a serious incident involving death and a causal or suspected causal link to the AI system. The duties therefore are not the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant actor to communicate information to an external recipient, but they concern different substantive duties: a processor must promptly inform the controller of a personal-data breach, whereas a deployer must notify the market-surveillance authority of the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment and submit a completed template.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The triggering events, actors, recipients, and information purposes differ: a personal-data breach and processor-to-controller incident notice versus completion of a high-risk AI fundamental-rights impact assessment and deployer-to-market-surveillance-authority notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not meaningfully the same because they involve different event families, different obligated actor roles, different recipients, and substantially different content and purposes; a shared broad verb of informing/notifying is insufficient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require organisational/operational capability relating to security or cyber-risk information, but A requires providers to implement proportionate technical, operational and organisational security measures, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain capabilities and personnel to collect and analyse information about vulnerabilities, threats and ICT incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive security-measures obligation imposed on public electronic communications providers; Norm B is an information-gathering and analytical-capacity obligation imposed on financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different core duties; the shared cyber/security subject matter does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen, en om de waarschijnlijke gevolgen ervan voor hun digitale operationele weerbaarheid te analyseren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity providing a trust service to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, promptly and within 24 hours where necessary. B requires the governing body of a financial entity to establish and oversee ICT-risk governance and enterprise-level reporting channels for obtaining information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, planned material changes, impacts on critical or important functions, serious ICT-related incidents, and response, recovery, and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-notification duty imposed on a trust-service provider and directed to external authorities/CSIRT; B is an ongoing governance and information-channel duty imposed on a financial entity’s governing body, with no specified external recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A requires an external significant-incident report, whereas B requires governance, oversight, and internal information-channel arrangements. The shared ICT-incident subject matter is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communications relating to serious ICT/AI incidents, but Norm A requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties and potentially the public, whereas Norm B requires a time-bound incident notification after a death where a causal link or suspected link to a high-risk AI system exists.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing planning and disclosure-capability obligation directed to clients/counterparties/public; Norm B is an event-triggered notification obligation, with a specific death-related trigger and a ten-day maximum deadline, apparently under the AI Act's incident-reporting framework.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different underlying action/purpose: maintaining a crisis-communication plan enabling responsible disclosure is not the same compliance work as making a prescribed serious-incident notification within a statutory deadline. The shared serious-incident theme is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an actor responding to an incident, but Norm A requires reporting each significant incident, whereas Norm B requires the provider to investigate a serious incident, assess its risks, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and observe a restriction on modifying the AI system during the investigation. The reporting duty referenced in Norm B is in the related paragraph and is not the action imposed by Norm B itself.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty for essential or important entities under Articles 26–29; Norm B is an urgent post-report investigation and remediation duty for providers of high-risk AI systems, with cooperation and procedural safeguards.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and actor roles differ: Norm A imposes incident reporting on essential or important entities, while Norm B imposes investigation and corrective-action duties on providers of high-risk AI systems. verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires promptly notifying the affected data subject of a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy; B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for promptly detecting anomalous activities, ICT-performance issues, ICT-related incidents, and physical single points of failure.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the verb and actor-role level: A requires notifying a data subject, while B requires maintaining and testing detection mechanisms. The shared incident/security context is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions relate broadly to responding to cyber/ICT threats or incidents, but Norm A imposes an urgent information duty on an entity toward potentially affected service recipients, whereas Norm B primarily describes supervisory feedback and confirms that the financial entity remains responsible for reported ICT incidents. Norm B does not impose the same reporting or notification action on the regulated entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to inform potentially affected service recipients about protective measures and, if necessary, the significant cyber threat. Norm B concerns the competent authority's feedback after receiving an incident notification and the financial entity's continuing responsibility for handling the incident and its consequences.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core action differ: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to notify its service recipients; Norm B concerns supervisory feedback following a financial entity's prior incident report and states continuing responsibility, without imposing the same notification duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident compliance involving a financial/essential entity and competent authorities, but A requires an immediate early-warning report about a significant incident, whereas B requires sharing, on request, changes implemented after a post-incident evaluation.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role, with materially different substantive reporting regimes and insufficient textual basis to treat the reports as the same compliance work; the different recipient alone is not decisive.

verdict.evidence_span_b: doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern documenting or managing ICT/data-security risks or incidents, but A requires the controller to document personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, whereas B requires certain financial entities to incorporate operational conclusions from tests and post-incident analysis into their ICT-risk-assessment process.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a personal-data-breach notification containing specified information to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and affected person(s). De meldplicht van norm B omvat daarnaast specifieke ontvangers (markttoezichtautoriteiten), onmiddellijke melding en uiterlijktermijnen, en vervolgonderzoek/samenwerking; norm A verwijst voor procedure en inhoud naar de artikelen 26–29.

verdict.criterion_fired: Zelfde meldingshandeling, incidentfamilie en vergelijkbare gereguleerde actorrol, maar onvoldoende inhoudelijke gelijkheid voor DUPLICATE_BURDEN: de incidentcategorieën, toepasselijke actoren, ontvangers en aanvullende meldings-/onderzoeksvereisten verschillen. De verschillende ontvanger maakt het niet op zichzelf verschillend, maar hier is de inhoudelijke overlap slechts middelmatig.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responses to risks or incidents affecting digital-system security, but A requires compliance with a ministerial product/service-use restriction, whereas B requires reporting serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive procurement/use restriction imposed by a minister; Norm B is an incident-reporting, investigation, and cooperation duty imposed on high-risk AI-system providers.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and duty-bearing actor roles differ: A concerns an essential or important entity being required to use products or services from permitted suppliers, while B concerns providers reporting serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities. Similar security-risk/incident context and an authority addressee do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to communicate a qualifying personal-data breach to the data subject without undue delay. B requires the management body of a financial entity to establish corporate reporting channels enabling it to obtain information about ICT third-party arrangements, planned material changes, effects on critical or important functions, serious ICT-related incidents, consequences, and response, recovery, and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-triggered external breach communication to the affected data subject; B is an ongoing internal governance and information-gathering arrangement concerning ICT risk and third-party ICT services, not a duty to communicate a particular breach to a recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action, event-triggered duty, or actor role. A concerns communicating a personal-data breach to the data subject; B concerns the management body's governance responsibility and establishment of internal reporting channels for ICT-risk information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures to manage service-security risks and reduce the effects of security incidents. B requires reporting serious AI-system incidents to Member State market-surveillance authorities, within the applicable deadline (normally immediately and no later than 15 days, with shorter or special deadlines in specified cases).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a preventive security-measures obligation for public electronic-communications providers; B is a post-incident notification obligation for providers or, where applicable, deployers of high-risk AI systems, directed to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires implementing security measures, while B requires reporting serious AI incidents. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve an entity providing information to a competent authority concerning an ICT/security incident, but Norm A requires an incident notification with specified incident details, while Norm B requires, only upon request, an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate incident-reporting duty to the CSIRT and competent authority, including incident assessment, compromise indicators, and cross-border-impact information. Norm B is a request-based provision of an aggregated financial-loss estimate to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope and, principally, in the required action and content: Norm A requires prompt notification of a significant incident by an essential or important entity, whereas Norm B requires other-than-micro financial entities to provide a requested estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires entities to implement and maintain broad cybersecurity risk-management measures protecting network and information systems against incidents; B states that financial entities remain responsible for handling and consequences of ICT-related incidents already reported under Article 19(1), while the authority may provide feedback. verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties differ: A requires implementing preventive and organizational cybersecurity measures, whereas B preserves the financial entity's responsibility for handling and consequences of already-reported ICT incidents. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different core actions and concern different triggering structures: incident notification to authorities versus ongoing ICT-risk identification and assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions authorize the relevant minister to make further implementing rules; neither provision itself imposes a substantive reporting, notification, retention, or information duty on the regulated actor.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern powers of public authorities to impose sanctions or corrective measures, but neither imposes the same concrete compliance action on the regulated entity. Norm A specifically empowers a supervisory authority to impose an administrative fine under GDPR Article 83; Norm B grants competent authorities broad supervisory, investigative, and sanctioning powers under DORA.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a specific GDPR power to impose an administrative fine, whereas Norm B is a general allocation of supervisory, investigative, and sanctioning powers under DORA.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same duty on the same regulated actor: Norm A concerns a supervisory authority's specific power to fine for GDPR violations, while Norm B concerns competent authorities' general DORA powers. The apparent similarity is at the level of public enforcement powers, not duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern informing a recipient about an incident, but A concerns public disclosure of a significant incident (by the CSIRT/competent authority or compelled from the entity), whereas B concerns notifying the affected person about a personal-data breach, potentially compelled by the Dutch Data Protection Authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern the competent authority’s enforcement powers, including imposing administrative sanctions or fines; neither imposes an incident-reporting, notification, retention, or information-provision duty on the regulated entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A specifically authorizes a competent authority to impose an administrative fine on an important entity for violating Article 5:20(1) of the General Administrative Law Act, with the related paragraph specifying that this may occur together with or after a warning or other listed enforcement measures. Norm B grants competent authorities broad supervisory, investigative, and sanction-imposition powers necessary to perform their duties under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions share the competent-authority enforcement role and sanctioning theme, but they do not impose the same compliance duty: A concerns a specific administrative fine for a specified violation, whereas B is a general grant of supervisory, investigative, and sanctioning powers under the Regulation. The triggering legal violations and operative scope are not the same, and no duplicated work by the regulated entity is required.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/data-security compliance in response to security risks or incidents, but Norm A is an exemption from notifying affected individuals after a personal-data breach, whereas Norm B requires covered financial entities to establish and maintain ICT-risk controls, including rapid identification of anomalies and handling of ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A removes a notification duty where effective protective measures make the breached personal data unintelligible; Norm B imposes ongoing ICT-risk-management and incident-detection/response measures on specified financial entities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor scope/role and core action: A concerns a provider’s conditional non-notification to the affected person, while B concerns specified financial entities’ ongoing implementation of ICT-risk-management measures. The shared security-incident context and broad digital-security subject matter do not create duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern regulatory handling of compliance matters, but A authorizes rules specifying the content and method of incident warnings/reports, while B empowers authorities to require corrective measures and obtain information during investigations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a rule-making provision about the formal requirements for warnings and reports; Norm B is an enforcement/investigatory power to demand corrective measures and access information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions do not impose the same underlying action on the same actor in response to the same event. A concerns delegated rules governing early warnings, notifications, interim reports and final reports; B concerns competent-authority investigative access and demands for corrective measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Impose an administrative fine for a legal violation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns enforcement against an essential entity for violations of the Dutch NIS2 implementation framework and related binding EU acts, whereas Norm B concerns enforcement by the Dutch data-protection authority for violations involving criminal-law personal-data processing, with specified maximum fine amounts.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions authorize different authorities to impose fines on different regulated actors for different categories of infringement; the shared fine mechanism is not the same underlying compliance duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern requiring the responsible entity to communicate a personal-data breach to the affected data subject when the breach has not already been communicated and the authority considers the relevant privacy/rights risk sufficient. However, GDPR Article 34 also incorporates exceptions or substitute measures under paragraph 3.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a public electronic communications service provider and an authority requiring notification where adverse privacy consequences are likely; Norm B concerns a controller and an authority assessing a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, with Article 34(3) exceptions or an alternative public communication measure.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same breach-notification-to-data-subject pattern, but different regulated actor roles and materially different risk tests and conditions mean the texts do not establish the same compliance duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A betreft het bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten (met een uitzondering voor bepaalde ondernemingen); norm B betreft het melden van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan een bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A bepaalt wanneer de registerplicht van artikel 30, leden 1 en 2, niet van toepassing is; norm B legt financiële entiteiten een incidentrapportageplicht op, met voorgeschreven kennisgevingen en verslagen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, het triggering event en de normadressaat verschillen wezenlijk: registerbeheer door verwerkingsverantwoordelijken/vertegenwoordigers versus rapportage van ernstige ICT-incidenten door financiële entiteiten aan een bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A concerns imposing a continuity obligation on a service to continue facilitating reliable electronic access after withdrawal. B concerns a supervisory authority imposing an administrative fine for GDPR infringements.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms address fundamentally different measures, actors, purposes, and triggering circumstances: continuity after withdrawal versus sanctions for data-protection infringements.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; the apparent similarity does not establish the same compliance obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern taking technical and organisational security measures in response to, or to mitigate the consequences of, security or personal-data incidents. However, Norm A imposes a general preventive security-risk-management duty on public electronic communications providers, while Norm B concerns measures that can exempt a controller from communicating a personal-data breach to data subjects (or require an alternative public communication).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general security-measures obligation for electronic communications providers; Norm B is a GDPR data-subject communication exception/alternative tied to a personal-data breach and high risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core legal action differ: Norm A requires communications providers to implement proportionate security measures generally, whereas Norm B addresses a controller’s breach-communication obligation and the conditions for avoiding or replacing that communication. Similar security-incident subject matter is insufficient for duplicate burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires certification bodies to conduct proper assessments leading to certification or withdrawal of certification; Norm B requires operators to ensure that affected AI systems they placed on the Union market undergo appropriate corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern fundamentally different regulatory functions and event families: conformity-certification assessment and possible withdrawal versus remediation of AI systems posing a risk.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core regulatory action/event: certification assessment or withdrawal by certification bodies versus corrective measures for risky AI systems by operators.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernhandeling, noch dezelfde actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie; A regelt niet-toepasselijkheid van verplichtingen, terwijl B een verzoek om aanmelding vereist.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responses to security or personal-data risks, but Norm A requires an authority-imposed restriction on using specified suppliers' products or services, whereas Norm B concerns notifying data subjects about a personal-data breach or applying an equivalent information measure, subject to exceptions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive national-security supply/use restriction imposed on an essential or important entity; Norm B is a data-subject communication duty or substitute measure following a personal-data breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering-event families, and duty-bearing actor roles differ materially; any broad security-related similarity does not create the same compliance work.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben noch dezelfde kernactie, noch hetzelfde triggering event of dezelfde actorrol. A ziet op registratie van verwerkingsactiviteiten; B op melding van ICT-incidenten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A betreft sanctionering wegens niet-naleving van een toezichthoudend bevel; norm B betreft een schriftelijke bevestiging en tijdelijke overdracht van monitoring/verantwoordelijkheid voor certificaten na schorsing of beperking.

Norm B legt juist een concrete bevestigings- en continuïteitsmaatregel op aan de aanbieder van het systeem, met een termijn van drie maanden en verzending aan nationale bevoegde autoriteiten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern public-authority enforcement activity, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Norm A concerns taking supervisory and enforcement measures in response to another Member State authority’s assistance request, while Norm B concerns ACM’s power to impose administrative enforcement orders or fines.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A governs cross-border supervisory assistance by a competent authority; Norm B allocates sanctioning powers to ACM, specifically an administrative enforcement order or administrative fine.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core enforcement function: cross-border assistance and supervisory measures versus ACM sanctioning authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A imposes a daily coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider until its obligations are fulfilled, for up to six months after notification of the fine decision. B requires a system provider, in a specified contingency, to confirm in writing to national competent authorities that another qualified notified body will temporarily monitor and assume responsibility for certificates during the suspension or restriction period.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The provisions concern fundamentally different legal mechanisms and duties: A is enforcement through a coercive fine imposed by a lead overseer; B is a conditional written confirmation and temporary transfer of certificate-monitoring responsibility by a system provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event family, and actor role; A concerns enforcement of obligations against a critical ICT service provider, whereas B concerns continuity of certificate monitoring after suspension or restriction and a confirmation to national authorities.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns ACM enforcement of specified provisions of the Dutch digital/data-law framework and permits a fine capped by the Dutch criminal-law sixth-category amount or 10% of the offender’s EU turnover. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity/provider to take corrective or remedial measures to remedy non-compliance after an authority identifies a regulatory deficiency, within an authority-prescribed period. However, Norm A concerns enforcement against essential entities under the NIS2 framework, while Norm B concerns an AI provider whose system is found to be high-risk under the AI Act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties arise in different regulatory regimes and concern different substantive objects and compliance requirements: essential-entity deficiencies under NIS2 versus conformity of an AI system with the AI Act. Norm A is also framed as an enforcement power requiring Member States to empower authorities, whereas Norm B directly requires the provider to bring the AI system into conformity and take corrective measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same corrective-action pattern, event family, and regulated-entity role, but different substantive regimes, objects, and compliance purposes; therefore the duties are related rather than the same work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance following an ICT/data-related incident, but Norm A creates an exception from notifying affected individuals, whereas Norm B requires post-incident evaluations, causal analysis, improvement identification, and—on request for certain entities—communication of implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns whether a personal-data-breach notification to the affected data subject is required, with an encryption-based exemption. Norm B concerns internal post-incident review and remediation, plus possible disclosure of resulting changes to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties differ: Norm A governs notification or exemption from notification to the person whose personal data are affected; Norm B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident evaluations and identify improvements, with certain entities sharing implemented changes with competent authorities on request. The shared incident-related context and broadly comparable regulated-entity setting do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid als bedoeld in artikel 11.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to issue an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours (with specified incident details and responsible-officer contact information). Norm B concerns an exemption from the obligation to maintain a register of processing activities; where the exemption does not apply, the related duty is to maintain a processing-activities register containing specified GDPR information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered, time-limited external warning/reporting duty. Norm B is a continuing record-keeping obligation concerning processing activities, subject to an employee-count and processing-risk/sensitivity exception; it has no recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action or concern the same triggering event: A requires rapid incident warning/reporting by an essential or important entity, while B addresses whether a controller or representative must maintain a processing-activities register.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben, tenzij het waarschijnlijk is dat de verwerking die zij verrichten een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkenen, de verwerking niet incidenteel is, of de verwerking bijzondere categorieën van gegevens, als bedoeld in artikel 9, lid 1, of persoonsgegevens in verband met strafrechtelijke veroordelingen en strafbare feiten als bedoeld in artikel 10 betreft.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern technical/organizational handling of ICT or data-security risk, but A concerns communicating a personal-data breach to affected data subjects (subject to exceptions), whereas B requires vulnerability assessments before deployment or redeployment of specified ICT applications, infrastructure, or supporting ICT services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a data-subject breach-communication rule and its quoted text describes exceptions based on protective measures; Norm B is a preventive ICT-testing obligation requiring vulnerability assessments before deployment or redeployment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, and actor role: A relates to communicating a personal-data breach to data subjects, while B requires specified financial-market entities to conduct vulnerability assessments before ICT deployment or redeployment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions authorize the government to adopt further rules by general administrative order (algemene maatregel van bestuur); neither provision itself imposes a concrete reporting, notification, retention, or information-supply duty on the regulated actor.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns further rules about paragraphs 1–3 of an audit provision, with the related context indicating that the investigation is conducted in a manner prescribed by the competent authority. Norm B concerns further rules about an investigation, data provision, a cooperation obligation, and notification of data provision under paragraph 4–6. The delegated subject matter therefore differs substantially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions share only the legislative technique—authorizing further rules by algemene maatregel van bestuur—not the same underlying regulated compliance duty. Their subject matter, referenced obligations, and apparent actor roles differ; a duplicated burden is therefore not established.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires other financial entities (excluding micro-enterprises) to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive digital operational-resilience testing programme, using a risk-based approach and specified testing methods. Norm B requires operators to ensure that affected AI systems placed on the EU market undergo appropriate corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a proactive ICT-resilience testing-programme obligation for financial entities; Norm B is a corrective-measures obligation concerning affected AI systems already placed on the EU market.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, event family, and operative action: establishing and operating a resilience-testing programme versus ensuring corrective measures are applied to AI systems.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A wijst een minister aan als cybercrisisbeheerautoriteit en koppelt daaraan taken uit een nationaal cybercrisisplan; norm B verleent toezichthoudende autoriteiten corrigerende bevoegdheden, waaronder het gelasten dat een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke een persoonsgegevensinbreuk aan de betrokkene meedeelt.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft de institutionele aanwijzing en crisisbeheertaken van een overheidsautoriteit bij grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten. Norm B betreft een AVG-corrigerende bevoegdheid van een toezichthoudende autoriteit om een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke tot mededeling aan de betrokkene te gelasten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen leggen geen vergelijkbare verplichting aan dezelfde actor op en zien niet op dezelfde concrete gebeurtenis of compliancehandeling. A is een aanwijzings-/taaktoewijzingsnorm voor een cybercrisisbeheerautoriteit; B is een handhavingsbevoegdheid van een gegevensbeschermingstoezichthouder.

verdict.evidence_span_b: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke gelasten een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens aan de betrokkene mee te delen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires public electronic communications providers to implement technical, operational, and organisational security-risk measures. B is an applicability/exclusion rule stating that equivalent sector-specific EU requirements on cybersecurity risk-management measures or significant-incident reporting displace the Directive’s provisions for covered entities; it does not itself impose a matching operational duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive security-measures obligation for providers of public electronic communications networks or services. Norm B is a conflict-of-laws/scope rule concerning whether NIS2 provisions apply where equivalent sector-specific EU obligations exist; it does not prescribe the same measures or reporting work.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core compliance action: A requires implementation of security measures, whereas B determines non-application or continued application of Directive provisions and contains no direct duty to implement measures or report an incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern an administrative authority imposing an administrative fine as a possible enforcement/corrective measure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a national NIS2-related power to fine an important entity for specified statutory or directly applicable NIS2-related violations, whereas Norm B is a GDPR supervisory-authority power to fine under Article 83, alongside or instead of other GDPR corrective measures. They do not impose the same underlying duty on the regulated entity; they confer potentially overlapping enforcement powers on authorities under different legal regimes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions share the broad enforcement verb 'impose an administrative fine', but the regulated actors, legal regimes, violation categories, and enforcement purposes differ. Norm A addresses an important entity and NIS2/national-law violations; Norm B addresses a controller or processor and GDPR infringements. This is not duplicated compliance work by the same actor for the same event or content.

Norm B is a corrective enforcement power requiring a controller to notify the affected data subject of a personal-data breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not borne by the same actor: A concerns action by a CSIRT/competent authority or an entity compelled by it, whereas B concerns an order issued by a data-protection supervisory authority to a controller. Their purposes and audiences also differ: public disclosure for awareness, prevention, control, or general interest versus communication to the data subject as a corrective GDPR measure.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: NORM A bepaalt wanneer sectorspecifieke cyberbeveiligingsverplichtingen de relevante verplichtingen van deze richtlijn vervangen of uitsluiten; NORM B verplicht bepaalde financiële entiteiten een programma voor het testen van digitale operationele weerbaarheid vast te stellen, te handhaven en te evalueren.

verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben niet dezelfde kernhandeling, actorrol of gebeurtenisfamilie: A gaat over de niet-toepasselijkheid van NIS2-bepalingen bij gelijkwaardige sectorspecifieke regels, terwijl B een testprogramma voor digitale operationele weerbaarheid vereist.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn de relevante bepalingen van deze richtlijn, met inbegrip van de in hoofdstuk VII bedoelde toezichts- en handhavingsbepalingen, niet van toepassing op dergelijke entiteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen, rekening houdend met de criteria in artikel 4, lid 2, voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: bepaalt dat NIS2-verplichtingen en toezicht-/handhavingsbepalingen niet van toepassing zijn wanneer gelijkwaardige sectorspecifieke verplichtingen gelden. B: verplicht financiële entiteiten bij herstel of reconstructie na een ICT-gerelateerd incident controles en afstemmingen uit te voeren om gegevensintegriteit en consistentie te waarborgen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een toepasselijkheids-/vrijstellingsregel over de verhouding tussen sectorspecifieke EU-wetgeving en NIS2; norm B is een operationele herstel- en gegevensintegriteitsmaatregel voor financiële entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben wel een verwante incidentcontext en richten zich op financiële/essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten, maar leggen geen dezelfde verb-level compliance-actie op: A sluit verplichtingen uit onder bepaalde voorwaarden, terwijl B controles tijdens ICT-incidentherstel verplicht stelt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn de relevante bepalingen van deze richtlijn, met inbegrip van de in hoofdstuk VII bedoelde toezichts- en handhavingsbepalingen, niet van toepassing op dergelijke entiteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern measures following an incident, but A requires an entity to include specified information in an early warning about a significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B concerns whether a controller must communicate a personal-data breach to affected data subjects, with possible substitute measures or exemptions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an authority/CSIRT-facing early-warning information duty with a 24-hour deadline; B is a data-subject communication duty concerning a high-risk personal-data breach and possible exemptions or equivalent public information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action/recipient: A concerns an essential or important entity reporting a significant incident to authorities/CSIRT, while B concerns a controller communicating a personal-data breach to affected data subjects or using an equivalent public measure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: de mededeling zou onevenredige inspanningen vergen. In dat geval komt er in de plaats daarvan een openbare mededeling of een soortgelijke maatregel waarbij betrokkenen even doeltreffend worden geïnformeerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern the exercise of enforcement powers by a competent supervisory authority in response to regulatory non-compliance: imposing or requiring a corrective/enforcement measure. However, Norm A specifically authorizes the Dutch data-protection authority to impose an administrative fine, while Norm B concerns competent authorities’ power to require corrective measures for infringements of the DORA Regulation, with related procedural safeguards.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a specific administrative-fine power under GDPR Article 83 for the Dutch data-protection authority; Norm B is a broader DORA enforcement power to require corrective measures, including measures potentially directed at financial-entity management, with reasoned-decision and appeal requirements.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad enforcement/infringement context and comparable supervisory-authority role, but the operative measures differ materially: a capped administrative fine under Norm A versus requiring corrective measures for DORA infringements under Norm B. The texts do not establish that the same measure or identical compliance work must be performed twice.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Autoriteit persoonsgegevens kan in geval van overtreding van het bepaalde in artikel 83, vierde, vijfde of zesde lid, van de verordening een bestuurlijke boete opleggen van ten hoogste de in deze leden genoemde bedragen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: corrigerende maatregelen te eisen voor inbreuken op de voorschriften van deze verordening.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions authorize the imposition of an administrative fine for a legal violation; neither imposes a reporting, notification, retention, information-provision, or implementation duty on the regulated entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns the competent authority fining an essential entity for violating Article 5:20(1) of the General Administrative Law Act, whereas Norm B concerns the Minister fining specified persons connected with violations of listed provisions, with a maximum fifth-category criminal-law amount per violation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared verb-level action (imposing an administrative fine) is an enforcement power, but the provisions address different sanctioning authorities, different liable persons, and different underlying violations; they do not require the same compliance work to be repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit kan tevens aan een essentiële entiteit een bestuurlijke boete opleggen in geval van overtreding van artikel 5:20, eerste lid, van de Algemene wet bestuursrecht.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister kan degene die handelt in strijd met het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 9, vierde, zevende of achtste lid, 11, 13 en 14, tweede en derde lid, daartoe opdracht heeft gegeven of feitelijk leiding geeft aan de rechtspersoon die in strijd met het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 13, eerste, tweede, derde of vierde lid, een bestuurlijke boete opleggen van ten hoogste het bedrag dat is vastgesteld voor de vijfde categorie, bedoeld in artikel 23, vierde lid, van het Wetboek van Strafrecht, per overtreding die is begaan.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen regelen de bevoegdheid van een toezichthouder om een bestuurlijke/administratieve geldboete op te leggen aan een overheidsachtige entiteit; zij leggen niet dezelfde meldings-, informatie- of herstelactie aan die entiteit op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft overtredingen van artikel 83, vierde tot en met zesde lid, van de AVG door Nederlandse overheidsinstanties of overheidsorganen en noemt de AP als bevoegde boeteoplegger. Norm B betreft instellingen, organen en instanties van de Unie binnen het toepassingsgebied van de AI-verordening en geeft de EDPS beoordelingsfactoren voor het opleggen en bepalen van de hoogte van de boete.
verdict.criterion_fired: Zelfde sanctietype en vergelijkbare toezichthoudende actor/overheidsachtige adressaat, maar verschillende rechtsgrond, bevoegde autoriteit, toepassingsgebied en inhoudelijke beoordelingscriteria; de normen leggen geen identieke compliance-werkzaamheden op.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Autoriteit persoonsgegevens kan in geval van overtreding van het bepaalde in artikel 83, vierde, vijfde of zesde lid, van de verordening door een overheidsinstantie of een overheidsorgaan een bestuurlijke boete opleggen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De Europese Toezichthouder voor gegevensbescherming kan administratieve geldboeten opleggen aan instellingen, organen en instanties van de Unie die binnen het toepassingsgebied van deze verordening vallen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern an authority imposing an administrative fine, but Norm A authorizes the Dutch Minister to fine specified violators of listed provisions, while Norm B authorizes a supervisory authority to impose a GDPR administrative fine under Article 83 among corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a national enforcement power tied to violations of specifically listed provisions and permits a fine up to the fifth criminal-law category per violation; Norm B is a GDPR supervisory-authority power, exercised as appropriate alongside or instead of other corrective measures and governed by Article 83.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and distinct legal enforcement regimes: Norm A concerns the Minister fining persons responsible for specified statutory violations; Norm B concerns a GDPR supervisory authority imposing an Article 83 administrative fine. The similarity is at the level of an enforcement sanction, not duplicated compliance work by the regulated entity.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister kan degene die handelt in strijd met het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 9, vierde, zevende of achtste lid, 11, 13 en 14, tweede en derde lid, daartoe opdracht heeft gegeven of feitelijk leiding geeft aan de rechtspersoon die in strijd met het bepaalde bij of krachtens artikel 13, eerste, tweede, derde of vierde lid, een bestuurlijke boete opleggen
verdict.evidence_span_b: naargelang de omstandigheden van elke zaak, naast of in plaats van de in dit lid bedoelde maatregelen, een administratieve geldboete opleggen op grond van artikel 83

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations connected to an organisation’s activities, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Norm A requires urgent communication to service recipients about measures in response to a significant cyber threat; Norm B, read with its referenced paragraph, concerns maintaining a register of processing activities and defines an exemption from that record-keeping duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent outward communication to potentially affected service recipients about a significant cyber threat. Norm B concerns internal GDPR records of processing activities, with the quoted paragraph specifying when the record-keeping obligation does not apply.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in core action, triggering event, actor role, recipient, and compliance purpose; they do not require the same work to be repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A is an applicability/exemption rule: equivalent sector-specific cybersecurity risk-management or significant-incident-reporting requirements displace the NIS2 provisions for covered entities. Norm B requires an AI-system provider or, where applicable, deployer to report a serious or widespread incident to Member State market-surveillance authorities, immediately and no later than two days after awareness.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A does not itself impose a reporting duty; it determines whether NIS2 obligations and supervision/enforcement provisions apply where equivalent sector-specific rules exist. Norm B imposes a concrete serious-incident notification duty and deadline under the AI Act.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action or the same actor duty: A is a conflict-of-laws/non-application rule concerning essential or important entities, while B is an incident-reporting obligation for AI-system providers or, where applicable, deployers. The shared incident-related subject matter is insufficient to create duplicate reporting burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn de relevante bepalingen van deze richtlijn ... niet van toepassing op dergelijke entiteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident
